title: The two-zone 0.20x deep anchor is built only in _optimize_space_only; the DHW path's _solve_space never gets it
claim: The DHW path, which every default install runs, builds its own cold-start seed set in HeatPumpOptimizer._solve_space, and that set does not include the two-zone 0.20x baseline-energy anchor. Adding that anchor lowers the shipped objective on two-zone DHW-on winter cells by up to 0.2507 % (0.3396 objective units per day). The paired flat-price cells show 0.0000 %.
mechanism: _optimize_space_only seeds from the baseline thermostat: its power, plus bang-bang anchors at 1.0x and 0.35x of its energy, plus 0.20x for two-zone houses. _solve_space seeds instead from init_base: an init_base-shaped guess, bang-bang at init_base energy, headroom*0.5, and bang-bang at 0.35x init_base energy. So the DHW path has no baseline-power seed, keys its anchors on a different energy, and never gets the 0.20x under-heat anchor that round 7 found the price-driven two-zone optimum needs.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:_multi_start_minimize (the cold-start call from HeatPumpOptimizer._solve_space; read back through HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize(...).objective_value)
phenomenon_property: Every cold-start _multi_start_minimize call for a given topology should get the same structural seed set, keyed on the same baseline energy, whichever solve path (space-only or DHW) makes the call.
proposed_fix_scope: Build the cold-start structural seeds once, in a helper keyed on the baseline thermostat energy (baseline power, 1.0x, 0.35x, and 0.20x for two-zone). Call it from both _optimize_space_only and _solve_space; this means computing _compute_baseline_power before the DHW path's space solve. Add a DHW-on two-zone winter cell to tests/optimality.py's _CERT_CELLS so the DHW path is certified at all; today every certificate cell is DHW-off.

title: L-BFGS-B ftol=1e-6 stops the solve and its in-loop restart short of their own fixed point
claim: On two|dhw|summer_typical|winter_cold at 48 h, production's own L-BFGS-B restarted from the shipped plan at ftol=1e-12 lowers the recorded objective by 0.6507 % (55.3274 to 54.9674) at equal comfort.
mechanism: Every main run stops on RELATIVE REDUCTION OF F <= FACTR*EPSMCH after 8-36 iterations on 192 variables; _lbfgsb_restart then stops after 1 iteration on the same test, so the in-loop polish adopts nothing.
phenomenon_property: The shipped plan is a fixed point of production's own L-BFGS-B (same objective, bounds and jac) to within a relative 1e-4.
proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py _multi_start_minimize / _lbfgsb_restart stop rule (ftol) or a gradient-norm-based stop; weigh against the recorded #1293 refusal (tests/optimality.py claim for one|shoulder|winter_cold).

title: Multi-start seed set misses lower basins on shoulder prices, above the flat-price null
claim: On the 24 h shoulder-price grid (16 cells, excluding summer_warm), the production seed set's plan is beaten by the recorded candidates plus an Emax-fraction bang-bang ladder by up to 1.2012 % (mean 0.3909 %, 8 of 16 cells over 0.1 %) at equal comfort, against a flat-price null of at most 0.3247 % (mean 0.0918 %).
mechanism: The objective landscape is rugged: on one|nodhw|shoulder|shoulder, single seeds refine to between -3.5 % and +1.2 % of the shipped objective. Production's four or five energy-anchored starts all descend into a ~7.2 kWh basin, while an 8.5 kWh basin is reached only from seeds unrelated to the baseline energy (for example 0.8*Emax). The 1.25-2.0x baseline anchors do not reach it.
phenomenon_property: No start set reachable by a cheap structural seed family (bang-bang at any energy fraction) finds a lower objective than the shipped plan by more than the flat-price null.
proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py seed construction in _optimize_space_only/_solve_space: more diverse structural starts, weighed against the #1294 cost refusal; the baseline-multiple anchors alone do not close it (anchor.py).

title: A tz-naive persisted timestamp raises on every cycle at three sibling loader seams (snapshots, curve, comfort)
claim: With the stored timestamp written tz-naive, SnapshotRing.due, CurveLearner._step_down and ComfortLearner._decay raise TypeError on every call after load (21/21 heartbeats, 19/21 curve days, 21/21 comfort calls), and the #42 ring takes 0 snapshots instead of 3.
mechanism: The loaders parse with datetime.fromisoformat and keep a naive value; consumers subtract it from an aware now. drift.Cusum.load (naive->UTC) and AccuracyTracker.from_dict lead_pending (drop naive) already guard the same leaf class; these three siblings do not. The heartbeat call site swallows at DEBUG, so the snapshot insurance, bias alarm and rollback stop permanently and silently; with comfort learning on, climate set_temperature raises after the write, and _record_quiet_comfort_period raises inside async_run_optimization's except-Exception (read, not reproduced end-to-end).
phenomenon_property: No persisted timestamp reaches arithmetic against an aware clock without being normalised to aware at load.
proposed_fix_scope: In SnapshotRing.due (or from_dict), CurveLearner.from_dict and ComfortLearner.from_dict, normalise a naive parsed time to UTC as drift.Cusum.load does (or drop it as accuracy lead_pending does); one line each.

title: A non-numeric snapshot temperature_bias makes best_restore raise and suppresses the accuracy_drift issue for good
claim: For 4/4 JSON-legal non-numeric bias leaves ("0.3", "garbage", [0.3], {"v":0.3}) the restore_learned_snapshot service raises and 10 out-of-band days end with no accuracy_drift repair issue; 0/4 with a numeric leaf.
mechanism: SnapshotRing.from_dict only checks each snapshot is a dict; best_restore calls np.isfinite(bias), which raises TypeError on str/list/dict (QuarantiningStore passes finite numeric strings through). On the alarm day the heartbeat raises before _create_issue; the latch is already set so observe_bias never reports a change again.
phenomenon_property: Every snapshot leaf read by best_restore/due/observe_bias is type-validated at load or read under a guard, so no stored snapshot can make the #42 path raise.
proposed_fix_scope: snapshots.py: coerce bias with a guarded float() in best_restore (skip on failure), or validate accuracy.temperature_bias in from_dict.

title: One out-of-range DHW thermometer sample is booked as a physically impossible draw and inflates the published p90
claim: A single -127 C sample on day 4 folds a 42.218 kWh draw occurrence (control 1.073) and raises the published window p90 from 1.073 to 25.760 kWh; 1e6 folds 231757 kWh.
mechanism: async_learn_dynamics feeds the raw drop into async_fold_draw_stats (intensity*dt*thermal mass) with no plausibility bound; the occurrence stays in the 40-occurrence reservoir, and p90 is published as dhw_draw_stats.p90_kwh and, with DHW quantile targets on, becomes the plan's readiness energy.
phenomenon_property: Energy attributed to a tick or occurrence never exceeds what the tank can physically deliver (thermal mass x usable delta), whatever the thermometer reports.
proposed_fix_scope: dhw_learning.py: cap the per-tick attributed drop/energy by the tank's physical capacity (or reject a tick whose |dT/dt| exceeds a physical bound) before async_learn_usage/async_fold_draw_stats.

title: A timestamp stored while the clock ran ahead is trusted verbatim and stretches stale timeouts by the clock error
claim: After a clock that ran 30 days ahead is corrected, the open-window latch release, the weekly snapshot and the curve step first act on days 33/37/31 instead of 4/8/2 (365 days ahead: 369/373/366).
mechanism: Cusum.release_if_starved, SnapshotRing.due and CurveLearner._step_down compare now with a persisted time and never question one in the future; the vent latch it pins freezes every learner.
phenomenon_property: A persisted timestamp later than now is clamped or treated as unknown, so no timeout outlives its design by the clock error.
proposed_fix_scope: Clamp a loaded future timestamp to now (or treat as None) in Cusum.load, SnapshotRing.due and CurveLearner._step_down.

title: A malformed weather-forecast response wedges every later cycle until restart
claim: One weather.get_forecasts response whose forecast holds a non-dict row or is not a list makes every later _async_update_data raise UpdateFailed, even after the weather entity returns a healthy forecast again.
mechanism: _fetch_weather_forecast stores result[entity]['forecast'] into self._weather_forecast (via _forecast_in_model_units, which returns it untouched for a degC/m-s/mm entity) before validating row types; the solar loop then raises AttributeError, which the fetch's except marks as a failed fetch but leaves the stored forecast in place. On the next cycle _update_current_state -> _current_humidity iterates self._weather_forecast with entry.get BEFORE the fetch that would replace it, so the cycle aborts and the fetch is never reached again.
phenomenon_property: A weather forecast the coordinator stores can never make a later cycle fail: whatever a get_forecasts response holds, the stored forecast is a list of dict rows (or the previous/empty forecast), and a healthy response always recovers the next cycle.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._fetch_weather_forecast: validate forecast is a list and keep only Mapping rows before assigning self._weather_forecast (and treat an empty result as a failed fetch); optionally make _current_humidity/_forecast_arrays tolerate a non-dict row.

title: Finite-but-absurd weather forecast values reach the solve unbounded: failed plans and a runaway solve
claim: A single get_forecasts row with temperature -1e308 makes the plan fail while the cycle reports success, and a single row with wind_speed >= 1e12 makes the real process-worker solve run past a 60 s cap (healthy 3.45 s); clipping the rows where they are stored removes both.
mechanism: No physical-range bound sits between the forecast rows and _forecast_arrays; the arrays go straight to _await_optimize. Wind feeds thermal_model._stability_substeps, whose substep count grows with the wind-driven heat loss, so an absurd wind makes the per-step loop effectively unbounded; an absurd temperature leaves the optimizer no usable start.
phenomenon_property: Every forecast series handed to the solve is finite and inside a physical range, whatever the weather entity returns.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: bound temperature/wind/precipitation/irradiance rows to physical ranges (or drop the row) where the forecast is stored; lead to D1-s4 for the unbounded substep count in thermal_model._stability_substeps.

title: A sample count past 2**64 in the thermal-learning store fails every cycle, across restarts
claim: A JSON number >= 2**64 (e.g. 1e20 or 1e308, both accepted by Home Assistant's orjson Store) at cop_baseline[*][1] or capacity_envelope[*][1] makes every cycle raise TypeError in _learning_view.
mechanism: _async_load_thermal_learning / _load_t4b_learners coerce the count with int(entry[1]) and no bound; the resulting Python int exceeds int64 and _learning_view's np.isfinite(entry[1]) raises inside _build_data_dict every cycle. orjson refuses the >64-bit int on re-save, so the corrupt store is never overwritten.
phenomenon_property: No value a Home Assistant Store can hand a loader can make a later cycle fail; integer counts from a store are bounded to a range numpy accepts (or the entry is dropped) at load.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._async_load_thermal_learning/_load_t4b_learners: reject counts that are not finite or exceed a sane bound (e.g. 2**31) when parsing cop_baseline and capacity_envelope entries.

title: Five cycle-path guards swallow a persistent failure at DEBUG, including pump and frequency actuation
claim: A persistent exception in any of _command_frequency, _async_drive_pumps, _async_watch_learning_drift, _maybe_run_fuse_advisor or _maybe_refresh_price_tile produces zero WARNING-or-above records and zero repair issues over three cycles, while every cycle reports last_update_success=True.
mechanism: The callers fence each callee with `except Exception as err: _LOGGER.debug(...)`, every cycle, with no once-per-cause escalation or repair issue; at default log level the failure is invisible, so a programming error silently stops frequency and pump actuation.
phenomenon_property: A swallowed failure that repeats is visible to the user: at least one WARNING (or a repair issue) per distinct cause, while the cycle still completes.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: log the first occurrence of each distinct swallowed cause at WARNING (DEBUG on repeats), as _note_worker_fallback already does; consider a repair issue for the actuation sites.

title: Home Assistant stop waits out an in-flight solve before reaping the solve worker
claim: The EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener from async_register_worker_shutdown, fired 0.1 s into a real solve, returns only when the solve does (0.93 of the solve's duration), against 0.008 s with no solve in flight.
mechanism: _shutdown_process_pool takes the module-global _PROCESS_LOCK, which _run_in_process holds for the whole transport round trip (pickle.dump .. pickle.load, i.e. the entire solve). The reap therefore queues behind the solve instead of terminating the child; on a Pi (30-70 s solves, or the D1-s2-02 runaway) that is how long a restart stalls.
phenomenon_property: Reaping the solve worker at stop never waits for a solve in flight: the stop reap completes in bounded time independent of solve duration.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._shutdown_process_pool: grab the worker handle without waiting on the transport lock (or kill the child first so the in-flight pickle.load fails fast), keeping the lock only for the handle swap.

title: A tz-less return_time (card datetime-local) or a naive stored datetime wedges every cycle with TypeError
claim: A set_away return_time without an offset (the card's <input type=datetime-local> value, and services.yaml's own example) makes away.expire_override compare naive with aware; every later solve then returns solve_failed (2 of 2), and _resolve_away raises on 6 of 6 cycles, until away is switched off.
mechanism: away._parse_return_time returns datetime.fromisoformat(value) unnormalised. async_set_away stores the naive ISO string before expire_override raises, so every coordinator._resolve_away inside async_run_optimization raises and is fenced into 'solve_failed' with an ERROR traceback. The same unnormalised parse sits in legionella async_load (dt_util.parse_datetime, consumed by async_track's now - previous), in pump_arbiter._load (datetime.fromisoformat, consumed by hold()'s now - at, which escapes _apply_action as UpdateFailed) and in boost._parse_until (restore raises once). manual_plan._coerce_awareness is the sibling seam that guards it.
phenomenon_property: Every ISO datetime entering from outside the process (service input or persisted store) is normalised to an aware instant before it is compared or subtracted with dt_util.now(); no such value can make a per-cycle path raise.
proposed_fix_scope: Normalise at each parse seam (away._parse_return_time, boost._parse_until, pump_arbiter._load, legionella.async_load) with dt_util.as_local for a naive result, or share manual_plan._coerce_awareness; one shared helper.

title: Pump-duty arbiter re-registers its timer and state listener on an unloaded coordinator and keeps writing the pump
claim: A pump state change dispatched just before unload leaves 2 live arbiter registrations on the torn-down coordinator after async_shutdown, and the leaked 1-minute tick writes the pump (2 writes) after the unload.
mechanism: pump_arbiter._changed queues hass.async_create_task(apply(coord)). async_shutdown -> pump_arbiter.release -> release_listeners empties held.unsubs. The queued apply then runs; it never checks coord._entry_released, and _listen sees empty unsubs, so it registers async_track_time_interval(_tick, 1 min) and async_track_state_change_event again. Nothing unsubscribes them, so the dead instance commands the pump every minute alongside the reloaded one, or after the integration is disabled.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.pump_arbiter:apply / pump_arbiter:_listen (driven via HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown on a real asyncio loop)
phenomenon_property: After async_shutdown returns, no arbiter registration references the coordinator and no arbiter path can write the pump; apply() declines once the entry is released.
proposed_fix_scope: pump_arbiter.apply (and _tick/_changed) return early when coord._entry_released; release() marks held as released so _listen refuses to re-arm.

title: pump_arbiter._load installs non-numeric set-point values that raise TypeError on every apply
claim: 8 of 200 seeded pump_duty store mutants (a string, list or dict set-point) make pump_arbiter.apply raise on every cycle, on both the aware and the naive clock, because _load type-checks nothing in pair[0].
mechanism: _load accepts held.written[slot] = (pair[0], fromisoformat(pair[1])). hold() -> _differs computes abs(observed - value) with a str/list/dict value and raises TypeError before _write can overwrite the record, so the corrupt record persists. The raise escapes coordinator._apply_action, so the whole update fails. Separately, 34 of 200 mutants make the loader itself raise KeyError/AttributeError once ('written' not a dict, pair a dict).
phenomenon_property: A persisted pump_duty record whose values are not the type the arbiter writes is dropped at load with one log line; no stored value can make apply() raise.
proposed_fix_scope: Validate each (value, at) pair in pump_arbiter._load (type per slot, aware stamp), catch KeyError/AttributeError, and log once.

title: Climate entity publishes the away setback as the user's target while the solve is in the executor
claim: With away active, a state write during the solve's executor await (the peak guard's async_update_listeners) publishes climate target_temperature 16.0 C against the configured 21.0 C, a 5.00 C deviation; after the solve it is 0.
mechanism: away.apply_setback writes the setback into the live ctx._opt_config.target_temp before _await_optimize, and restore_setback undoes it only after the await. HeatPumpOptimizerClimate.target_temperature ('the comfort target the user asked for') reads coordinator.target_temperature, which is that live field, so any loop-side state write in the window publishes the setback to the state machine and the recorder.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.climate:HeatPumpOptimizerClimate.target_temperature (window opened by away:apply_setback, write issued by coordinator._async_peak_guard_transition at coordinator._await_optimize)
phenomenon_property: A published entity value never reflects the solve-scoped envelope (setback, economy/open-window floor) that apply_setback/lower_floor write into the live config; readers see the configured value throughout the solve.
proposed_fix_scope: Apply the away envelope to the solve's deep-copied opt_config (after _solve_snapshot) instead of the live one, or have climate.target_temperature read the configured target.

title: Boost 'two-hour maximum' is an absolute instant: a clock step back or a far-future store extends it without bound
claim: A space boost (nameplate power, comfort ceiling, full displace) stays live 2+J hours after the wall clock steps back J hours (J=24 gives 26.0 h), and a restored until in 2099 never expires (72.0 h at the harness cap).
mechanism: BoostState.expire/active compare the stored until with now only, and boost.restore accepts any parsed until > now; nothing bounds until - now by BOOST_HOURS.
phenomenon_property: A boost channel is never live more than BOOST_HOURS after any instant at which it is read, whatever the clock does or the store holds.
proposed_fix_scope: Clamp until to now + BOOST_HOURS in BoostState.expire/active and in restore.

title: FrequencyMap.from_dict admits an unbounded ratio or out-of-range decile that pins recommend() at hz_min for days
claim: 10 of 200 seeded frequency-map store mutants (a huge ratio, or a negative decile key with a large ratio) leave the compressor recommendation for a 3 kW target at hz_min, delivering under 50 %, even after 96 truthful folds.
mechanism: from_dict refuses non-finite or non-positive ratios and negative counts, but accepts any int key and any finite ratio. recommend() walks buckets ascending; a phantom bucket predicting ratio*mid >= target at or below hz_min answers first, and _command_frequency clips it to hz_min. observe() only decays the ratio with EWMA alpha 0.1, so a 1e308 ratio needs thousands of folds.
phenomenon_property: A loaded frequency map contains only deciles in [0, FREQ_DECILES) with physically plausible kW/Hz ratios; no stored bucket can pin the recommendation outside what the healthy map would answer.
proposed_fix_scope: Bound the key to range(FREQ_DECILES) and the ratio to a plausible ceiling in FrequencyMap.from_dict.

title: DefrostDerate.from_dict admits non-finite/out-of-range duty; the bucket pins at DERATE_MIN and never recovers
claim: A stored defrost duty cell that is non-finite (the strings "nan"/"inf" pass float()) or outside [0, 1] is loaded unchanged, silently, and pins that bucket's derate at DERATE_MIN=0.55 for the life of the process: 200 healthy zero-duty folds leave it at 0.5500 where a healthy bucket reaches 1.0000.
mechanism: _grid_of("duty", float) only casts; the factors grid beside it is re-clamped to [DERATE_MIN, DERATE_MAX] on load but duty is not. derate_from_duty maps NaN/huge duty to the 0.55 floor, and observe_duty's EWMA (0.9*current + 0.1*duty) keeps NaN/inf forever and needs thousands of folds to bring 1e300 below the 0.30 cap. No log line is emitted.
phenomenon_property: Every grid DefrostDerate.from_dict restores is bounded on load to the range its own learner can produce (duty in [0,1] and finite, counts >= 0), so no stored value can put a bucket where observe/observe_duty cannot move it back.
proposed_fix_scope: defrost.py DefrostDerate.from_dict: cast duty cells through a finite, [0,1]-clamped cast (as factors already are); optionally counts through max(0, int).

title: A failed solve is returned as a plan with status 'failed (...)', so the coordinator counts it a success
claim: When every L-BFGS-B start raises (or a single non-finite horizon input makes every start score non-finite), HeatPumpOptimizer's guards return a normal OptimizationResult whose status is 'failed (...)'; async_run_optimization publishes it as the plan, resets _solve_failures to 0 and never raises the solve_failures repair issue -- 0 failures and 0 issues after 3 such cycles, against 3 and 1 when the same fault is raised outside the guard.
mechanism: The try/except in _optimize_space_only (optimizer.py ~4025) and _solve_space (~3496) log ERROR and fall back to the initial heuristic power with status f'failed ({e})'. The coordinator decides 'the solve failed' by exception only, so it adopts the fallback, logs 'Optimization complete', and clears the failure streak and notice. One fact (did the solve fail) decided by two predicates.
phenomenon_property: Every path by which optimize() fails to solve surfaces to the caller as a failure (an exception or an explicit flag the coordinator's failure accounting reads), never as a plan it will adopt.
proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py: the two f'failed ({e})' guards either re-raise or mark the result so the coordinator's failure branch (coordinator.py async_run_optimization) treats it as a failed solve; which side owns it is the fixer's call (the coordinator side is D1-s2's cell).

title: One unreadable cell in a v2 defrost store voids all 12 measured buckets and is labelled a pre-v5.3.0 upgrade
claim: A version-2 DefrostDerate payload with a single malformed duty or duty_counts cell loads with every bucket's measured duty discarded and migrated=True, logging 'a pre-v5.3.0 store was upgraded' -- 226 of 250 one-bad-cell payloads, 2712 measured buckets discarded.
mechanism: _grid_of returns None for the whole grid on one failed cast, and the else-branch sets migrated from the presence of factors without looking at version, so a corrupt v2 store is reported as a v1 upgrade (published in diagnostics) instead of a quarantined bucket.
phenomenon_property: A corrupt cell in a current-version store is quarantined at its bucket and reported as corruption, never as a schema upgrade.
proposed_fix_scope: defrost.py from_dict: per-cell cast with a per-bucket reset, and set migrated only for a payload without version 2.

title: inputs.age_of ignores last_reported and accepts future stamps, diverging from InputReader's freshness rule
claim: A live sensor that re-reports an unchanged value is delivered as None (stale) by both age_of consumers once last_updated exceeds the limit, and a stamp ahead of the clock is delivered as fresh; InputReader judges the same State objects the opposite way in 13 of 18 cells.
mechanism: age_of (inputs.py) reads last_updated/last_changed only and returns a negative timedelta for a future stamp, which callers compare as `age > limit` and so treat as fresh. InputReader._age_minutes prefers last_reported and returns None for a future stamp (#775). The fix was made in the reader and never ported to its sibling.
phenomenon_property: Every freshness decision on a Home Assistant state must use the same stamp precedence (last_reported first) and the same future-stamp refusal as InputReader._age_minutes.
proposed_fix_scope: inputs.age_of: use the reader's stamp precedence and refuse a negative age (or delegate to one shared helper); add a test with last_reported != last_updated and a future stamp for both consumers.

title: Learner-store loaders check finiteness but not the domain their own update path enforces (price shape, peak tracker)
claim: Out of 300 seeded store mutants, 11 price-model and 8 peak-tracker mutants load silently (no WARNING) and make the next cycle deliver values no honest learner can produce: unpublished-step prices of 0 or more than 1000x the known mean, and a negative peak threshold or billed peak. 9 and 2 of them are still invalid one cycle later.
mechanism: PriceShapeModel.from_dict rejects only non-finite bins, but observe_day/observe_day_quarters clip bins to [SHAPE_MIN,SHAPE_MAX] and [QUARTER_FACTOR_MIN,QUARTER_FACTOR_MAX] and renormalise, so a finite 0, negative or 1e300 bin loads and prices the tail through extend_price_series (max(0, negative) = 0). PeakTracker._stored_peaks drops non-finite peaks but keeps negative ones, which observe() never records; threshold_kw/billed_peak_kw then go negative, and coordinator.py:6992 publishes that.
phenomenon_property: A persisted learner state must be loaded into the domain its own update path can produce (the same clip and sign gates), or be reset with one log line; checking finiteness alone is not enough.
proposed_fix_scope: PriceShapeModel.from_dict: apply observe_*'s clip ranges and renormalisation, clamp days/quarter_days to >=0, and drop non-finite residual_var, with one WARNING on repair. _stored_peaks: drop negative peaks like non-finite ones. Validate _window_samples/_window_factor ranges.

title: One huge JSON integer drops a whole price fetch (entity and Tibber) or Open-Meteo refresh instead of one row
claim: With 24 valid price rows plus one row whose value is 10**400, pull_prices (entity source) and prices_from_tibber_payload raise OverflowError and deliver 0 rows, and the Open-Meteo refresh keeps 0 of 72 good samples. Every other malformed value, including the string '1e999', drops only its own row.
mechanism: price_model._raw_value and open_meteo._parse_block wrap float(raw) in except (TypeError, ValueError); float() of an int too large for a double raises OverflowError, which escapes the per-row drop. Price rows propagate to the coordinator's fetch-failed path, which fires again every cycle while the attribute persists. Open-Meteo rows reach the #1519 fence, which discards the whole series. The sibling tariff._stored_peaks already catches OverflowError ('a huge JSON int').
phenomenon_property: Every per-row numeric parse of external input must drop the row on any conversion failure, OverflowError included, and never fail the whole payload.
proposed_fix_scope: Catch OverflowError in price_model._raw_value and open_meteo._parse_block (and apply_price_adjustments), with a huge-int row in the parser tests.

title: One off-grid timestamp collapses Open-Meteo's inferred resolution and erases the whole solar horizon
claim: One extra hourly sample stamped 1 or 5 minutes off the grid makes OpenMeteoSolar.irradiance_for return None for 192 of 192 quarter-hour steps; 30 minutes off gives 94 of 192. The refresh reports success with no WARNING.
mechanism: _parse_block sets resolution = min(positive gaps), so one stray sample shrinks every sample's averaging span to that gap. mean_over then covers less than 50% of each 15-min step and returns None. The humidity and snowfall series use the same parser.
phenomenon_property: A resolution inferred from external timestamps must be robust to a single irregular sample; one stray stamp must not change the coverage of every other sample.
proposed_fix_scope: Infer the resolution from the modal or median gap, or drop samples off the dominant grid, in _parse_block; test with one stray stamp.

title: Euler sub-step guard judges each store's diagonal ratio only, so coupled stores in accepted configs diverge
claim: For configurations the config flow accepts, ThermalModel._stability_substeps leaves the per-substep Euler map with spectral radius > 1, and a zero-input 24 h trajectory diverges (69/3936 grid configs leave the passive envelope, 50 past 100 K; named point reaches -2.84e35 degC).
mechanism: _stability_substeps bounds each store's (sum of couplings)/C*h by EULER_STABILITY_MAX_RATIO=1.5, on the premise that Euler is stable up to 2 per store. For coupled RC stores the stiff eigenvalue reaches the sum of the diagonal terms (Gershgorin: |lambda| <= 2*max diag), so lambda*h reaches 3 and the update oscillates with growth. Example: house mass 0.5, loss 0.2, slab mass 0.5, slab transfer 5.0 -> n_sub=2, radius 1.525.
phenomenon_property: For every parameter set the config flow and service writes accept, the explicit-Euler sub-step chosen by _stability_substeps is contractive: the per-substep map of the coupled stores (including the valved emitter conductances) has spectral radius <= 1, so a passive trajectory stays inside [min T_out, max T0].
proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py _stability_substeps: judge rows at ratio 1.0 (the Gershgorin bound) or use the step matrix's spectral radius, and include ua_rad/ua_floor in the upper and slab rows when throttled. n_sub stays 1 for every shipped configuration, so no golden drift is expected.

title: DHW refill coil debits the wood tank the full coil heat but spares the DHW tank only its scaled share
claim: In simulate_trajectory_with_dhw with the wood coil active, for a DHW tank below DHW_MIXED_USE_TEMP, the wood tank loses more heat than the coil spares the DHW tank (non-zero in 28/28 cells, up to 0.406 kWh per 15-min step; 0.054 kWh at DHW 35 degC / wood 70 degC).
mechanism: dhw_coil_draw_reduction splits the nominal draw into reduced+coil==draw and the wood tank is debited coil. simulate_dhw_step then scales the reduced draw by min(1,(T-inlet)/(40-inlet)), so the DHW tank is spared only scale*coil. (1-scale)*coil vanishes per step. The tap water is the same with or without the coil, because the coil only preheats the refill.
phenomenon_property: Across the coil, the heat the wood tank loses equals the heat the DHW tank is spared, at every DHW tank temperature, i.e. total wood+DHW debit with the coil equals the debit without it.
proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py simulate_trajectory_with_dhw / dhw_coil_draw_reduction: debit the wood tank the coil heat on the same tank-temperature scale the DHW step applies to the draw (or apply the scale before the split). The optimizer's coil mirror (optimizer.py dhw_coil_draw_reduction call sites) must follow.

title: Settlement caps (slab_settlement_cap, hold_demand_kw) ignore the learned house_heat_loss_scale the dynamics apply
claim: optimizer.slab_settlement_cap and optimizer.hold_demand_kw size the steady-state demand from the raw zone losses. simulate_step multiplies those losses by house_heat_loss_scale (via effective_heat_loss_coefficient), and the sibling _buffer_charge_ceiling does the same. So at any learned scale other than 1, the 'sustaining' slab cap does not sustain the target: the room drifts at up to 1.44 K/h, the cap sits up to 13.5 K low (67.5 kWh of slab heat the terminal cost cannot see), and published predicted_savings are overstated by up to 13.4 currency at scale 2.
mechanism: slab_settlement_cap: q_demand = u*(target-out) - gains, with u = heat_loss_coefficient or lower_floor_heat_loss_learned and no house_heat_loss_scale. hold_demand_kw has the same omission. Both feed _settlement_caps, which feeds _terminal_cost (the objective) and _deferred_energy_cost (the published savings). The dynamics and _buffer_charge_ceiling (the latter explicitly: 'a learned-leaky house that omitted it here got an optimistic ceiling') apply the scale.
phenomenon_property: Every steady-state demand the optimizer's settlement and valuation compute must use the same effective heat-loss coefficient the dynamics simulate: raw losses x house_heat_loss_scale (and x wind/rain where applicable).
proposed_fix_scope: Multiply u_eff by params.house_heat_loss_scale in slab_settlement_cap (both branches) and hold_demand_kw, as _buffer_charge_ceiling does, or route them through ThermalModel.effective_heat_loss_coefficient. Expect golden drift only where a fixture sets the scale (default 1.0 leaves every fixture byte-identical).

title: #1067 flow-lift bias clamp (15 K) cannot reach real supply: model curve tops out at 27.9 C, COP overstated up to 37%
claim: With flow_curve_cop enabled, ThermalModel.compute_cop prices the direct-plant lift at curve_flow_temp + flow_curve_bias. The model's own curve never exceeds 27.9 C on the default houses, because emitter UA is derived from pump nameplate at a fixed 15 K, while the bias is clamped at FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K = 15 K. So a plant running at 40/45/50 C pins the bias at the clamp in every cell, and the priced COP exceeds the COP at the real supply by up to 8.4% / 22.8% / 36.8%.
mechanism: flow_lift.FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K is justified in its comment against a 35 C curve ('a fixed-setpoint plant running 45 C against a curve asking 35 C is 10 K out'). But curve_supply_temp -> flow_target_for_indoor -> mixing_valve.flow_setpoint uses emitter_ua = max_electrical_power*cop_nominal/emitter_design_delta_t (15 K, not configurable), which gives 22-28 C curves. Residuals of 17-27 K are real installation offsets against this curve, but the clamp truncates them.
phenomenon_property: The priced direct-plant supply (curve + learned bias) must be able to reach the measured supply for any real plant: the bias clamp must be sized against the model's own curve, not an assumed 35 C one.
proposed_fix_scope: Size FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K (or make it relative) against curve_supply_temp's actual range, e.g. clamp the priced flow to a plausible absolute supply band instead of a 15 K offset, or make emitter_design_delta_t configurable so the curve matches radiator plants. The flag is off by default, so no golden fixture moves except direct_flow_carnot if it enables the curve.

title: DHW-path savings settle-up replays space schedule without the DHW coil: end state differs from published trajectory

In the wood_coil golden scenario the settled end state is 0.42 K warmer in the wood tank (plus 0.06-0.09 K in room, upper, lower, slab and buffer), and published predicted_savings are overstated by 0.48 (0.31% of baseline).

title: _current_spot_price reads a quarter up to 45 min stale under 15-minute price entries

title: PV piecewise cost clipped by import_margin's zero floor wherever import price < export price
claim: pv.import_margin floors (import - export) at zero, so wherever import < export on a surplus step, HeatPumpOptimizer._energy_cost_fn and pv.blended_block_prices price surplus-covered energy at the import price instead of the export compensation it forgoes. This breaks the stated identity export·min(P,s)+import·max(P−s,0) on 16 of 96 steps for summer_negative at the shipped default export price 0.0. On a real solve the published predicted_cost is −0.609 where the identity gives 0.000, and the plan draws 5.07 kWh from surplus in negative-price steps against 2.27 kWh unfloored.
phenomenon_property: Every PV-aware pricing seam must charge surplus-covered energy at the export compensation for any sign of import − export; no seam may floor the margin.
proposed_fix_scope: Drop the clip in pv.import_margin, or replace it with a guard only on non-finite values. Correct its docstring's rationale: with export > import, the unfloored cost is still correct and does not invert anything. Add a features.py pin covering a negative-import surplus step and an export > import step through both _energy_cost_fn and blended_block_prices.

title: sysid adoption interval misses the true UA on 14 of 22 fits it admits; admitted fits biased high
claim: Under white room-sensor noise of 0.01-0.05 degC, 14 of the 22 two-state sysid fits that adoption_decision admits have the true UA outside their own 95 % interval (nominal ~5 %), and 21 of 22 over-estimate UA (mean +7.26 %, max +18.64 %).
mechanism: The gate admits only fits whose profile interval is finite and narrow; with the comfort-bounded collinear window the realisations that produce a sharp profile are a biased subset (ensemble 95 % half-width of log UA 0.15-0.27 against admitted reported 0.05-0.09). One contributor: _simulate_slab_path anchors the hidden stores' held state on the single noisy first reading, an error source the interval does not carry (anchor perturbation 0.636 -> 0.439). A free-heat prior mis-set by 0.2-0.4 kW is a second seam (typical_slab 3/12 and 2/6 admitted beyond the bar).
phenomenon_property: For every fit the gate admits, the combined half-width it reads must cover the true UA at its stated 95 % level under the noise the experiment is designed for; admitted fits must not carry a systematic sign of bias.
proposed_fix_scope: sysid.py: carry the first-reading (initial-state) uncertainty into the fit (estimate the initial offset or average the settle readings) and calibrate the adoption interval against an ensemble (e.g. inflate by the measured ensemble/Wald ratio or bootstrap) so admitted fits meet 95 % coverage; pin with a seeded coverage test.

title: sysid step sized to exactly the abort bound: sensor noise aborts 100 of 294 experiments, light_new 81 of 96
claim: With the plant's own max power, SystemIdentification._size_step_power targets a peak equal to max_excursion_c while step() aborts on the same bound, so white sensor noise of 0.01-0.05 degC aborts 100 of 294 experiments (light_new 81 of 96 noisy runs; 47 of 48 at the default 0.5 h cadence) before any fit runs.
mechanism: The sizer's fits() test is peak <= max_excursion_c (headroom only on two-zone plants, TWO_ZONE_SIZING_HEADROOM_C) and _over_excursion aborts on |reading - baseline| > max_excursion_c: a noiseless peak at the bound leaves no margin for the reading's noise.
phenomenon_property: A comfort-sized experiment must leave room for the sensor noise the fit is designed to tolerate; a noise level the estimator accepts must not abort the experiment that feeds it.
proposed_fix_scope: sysid.py: size against max_excursion_c minus a noise margin (e.g. a fixed headroom like TWO_ZONE_SIZING_HEADROOM_C on one zone too, or a multiple of the settle-phase reading scatter), keeping the abort bound unchanged.

title: Expert setup: the zones page says 'leave defaults if you don't need two-zone' and leaving them turns two-zone on

title: Per-row Python loop in _comfort_terms_batch costs 13-32% of every solve; a row-vectorized twin is bit-identical here
claim: HeatPumpOptimizer._comfort_terms_batch spends 0.134-0.321 of optimize() thread CPU (0.32 on every two-zone cell) in a per-row numpy loop, and a twin that does the same elementwise ops on the [B, n] batch and reduces with axis=1 returns bitwise-identical penalty and comfort arrays and the same plans on all 8 cells tested, at 0.012-0.039 of the solve.
mechanism: The batched gradient's 96 rows each re-enter ~11 np.sum plus ~10 elementwise numpy calls (two-zone) on 96-element arrays, so per-call Python/ufunc dispatch overhead, not arithmetic, is the cost: 501 gradient batches x 96 rows on the default two-zone DHW winter cell. The docstring keeps the loop for cross-backend bit parity; the measured twin gives 0 bit mismatches on x86_64, which is where the docstring says a batched reduction re-planned 19 of 51 stress scenarios.
phenomenon_property: A 'batched' cost term that re-enters numpy once per row of the batch pays per-call dispatch B times per gradient; every batched objective term must cost O(1) numpy calls per batch, not O(B), unless a measured bit-parity failure on a supported runner forbids it.
proposed_fix_scope: Replace the two per-row loops in _comfort_terms_batch with elementwise ops on the batch and np.sum(..., axis=1); keep the per-row twin as the test oracle and prove bit parity on CI's x86_64 AND arm64 runners (features.py #948 parity pins, stress work drift) before merging. Pi extrapolation (assumption: Pi-4 core ~4-6x this box for numpy-dispatch-bound Python): ~1.2-1.6 s saved per two-zone solve here -> ~5-9 s per solve on a Pi.

title: L-BFGS-B asks the scalar objective for f(x) every iterate at ~19-26x a batched row: 9-19% of the solve
claim: _multi_start_minimize hands scipy a scalar fun and a batched jac separately, so every iterate evaluates the scalar objective (1.0-1.6 ms, 18.6-25.9x one batched row) before the 96-row gradient batch; that scalar path is 0.087-0.192 of optimize() thread CPU, and serving f from an extra row 0 of the same batch (jac=True) drops it to 0.005-0.018 with every plan bitwise unchanged.
mechanism: scipy's ScalarFunction calls fun(x) then jac(x); the memo (#288) only saves the jac's f0 re-evaluation, not the scalar evaluation itself, which runs simulate_trajectory as a Python loop of simulate_step with a dataclasses.replace per step. The batched kernel's cost is per-call overhead amortised over rows, so a 97th row costs ~0.04-0.08 ms where the scalar call costs 1.0-1.6 ms. A one-row batch per scalar call is dearer still (recorded negative arm --via-batch: share 0.15 -> 0.31).
phenomenon_property: Where a batched objective exists, no L-BFGS-B iterate should pay a scalar full-horizon evaluation for f(x): f must come from the same batch as the gradient, bit-identical to the scalar objective.
proposed_fix_scope: In _multi_start_minimize and _lbfgsb_restart, when the batched jac serves the bounds, pass a fun that returns (f, g) with jac=True, f taken from row 0 of the gradient batch; keep the scalar objective for candidate scoring. Needs the same CI bit-parity proof as #97/#948 (row equals scalar objective). Pi extrapolation (assumption ~4-6x): ~0.7 s saved per two-zone winter solve here -> ~3-4 s on a Pi.

title: The sysid two-state fit runs inside one event-loop callback: 43-228 ms here (1.1-6x a reference solve)
claim: SystemIdentification.step, which the coordinator calls synchronously on the loop in _async_update_data, runs the whole identify_slab fit in the call that ends the relax phase: median 43 ms at the default 30-min cadence, 95 ms at 15 min, 228 ms at 5 min (1.14x, 2.46x, 5.95x tests/stress.py:reference_solve), against 0.17 ms for every other step call.
mechanism: _finish -> identify_slab (LM solve plus profile half-widths) is ordinary synchronous Python reached from step(); nothing in sysid hands it to an executor, and its cost grows with the sample count (the coordinator cadence).
phenomenon_property: No learner fit whose cost scales with its sample count may run synchronously in a coordinator cycle on the event loop; it belongs on the executor or the solve worker.
proposed_fix_scope: Run the fit (identify_slab via _finish) off the loop: have step() mark the experiment finished and let the coordinator await the fit through hass.async_add_executor_job (or the solve worker). Fires at most once per min_days_between_runs (30 days), hence low. Pi extrapolation (assumption ~4-6x): 43 ms -> ~0.2-0.3 s at the default cadence, 228 ms -> ~1-1.4 s at 5 min.

title: DHW min-run repair: a full-suffix re-simulation per refused weak slot, 12-23% of a single-zone DHW solve
claim: _apply_dhw_min_run makes 7,758 of the solve's 11,064 simulate_dhw_step calls on the single-zone DHW winter cell (0.17-0.23 of optimize() CPU on four single-zone cells), 81 % of its weak slots are refused, and stopping each refused slot's check at its first breaching chunk cuts the calls 26-40 % (7,758 -> 4,780) with every plan bitwise unchanged; at 48 h the calls grow 3.26x for 2x the horizon.
mechanism: Each weak slot extends the candidate trajectory from the slot to the end of the horizon (#1230's prefix reuse), and a refused slot then re-extends the base from the slot again, so the loop is O(weak x (n - slot)) Python steps; the refusal decision is already known at the first step that breaches.
phenomenon_property: A repair loop whose per-candidate verdict is decided at the first violated step must not simulate past that step; per-candidate work must be bounded by the distance to the verdict, not by the horizon.
proposed_fix_scope: In _apply_dhw_min_run, check the candidate incrementally and refuse at the first breach (the harness's early_exit is a working sketch); keep the full-suffix base refresh for refused slots. Plans are bit-identical by construction (same step function, same order); pin with the existing min-run features checks.

title: sensor_advisor ranking re-simulated on the event loop at every plan-sensor state write: 1152 simulate steps, ~32% of loop CPU per cycle
claim: Every state write of the two plan sensors (_PlanSensorBase.extra_state_attributes) calls topology.rank_sensor_advisor on the event loop. Each read of all entities makes 2 calls and 384 ThermalModel.simulate_step calls; with 3 writes per cycle that is 1152 loop-thread simulate steps and 31.6% of the cycle's loop-thread CPU, for a result that depends only on the config entry and the once-per-cycle heat_pump_power_series.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.topology:rank_sensor_advisor (called from sensor:_sensor_advisor_attribute in _PlanSensorBase.extra_state_attributes); heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_step counted outside executor jobs
phenomenon_property: No entity property evaluated at state-write time runs a thermal-model simulation. A value derived from configuration and per-cycle data is computed at most once per cycle, off the per-write path.
proposed_fix_scope: Compute the #1269 ranking once per cycle in the coordinator (e.g. in _build_data_dict, or memoised on the config plus the power-series tuple) and have both plan sensors read the cached value. The per-read ThermalParameters.from_config plus ThermalModel construction (0.54 ms per read even at 1 step) goes with it. Pi extrapolation: 8.4 ms/cycle here x ASSUMED 4-6x (Pi 4 Cortex-A72 vs this Xeon core, not measured) = 34-51 ms of event-loop CPU per 30-min cycle, plus more on every extra listener update (peak-guard transitions, snapshot restore).

title: No budgeted check can see a 2x of the coordinator's loop-thread work; nightly replay needs ~x5, stress.py reaches none of it
claim: An exact 2x of the coordinator cycle's loop-thread CPU (update work outside the executor plus the entity read) leaves tests/replay.py:cost_offenders empty: cycle_cpu_ratio goes 2.42 -> 2.82 against a 3.576 budget. tests/stress.py, the only per-PR CPU gate, executes 0 functions of coordinator.py/sensor.py/topology.py. Only a x5 of the loop work turns the nightly budget red.

HA writes every entity 3 times per cycle (2 listener updates in async_run_optimization plus the refresh's own), while replay times 1 read: loop_work.py measures 26.7 ms per real cycle against the ~14.9 ms replay budgets. Give it the same sqrt(2) band and a perturbation arm that doubles only that share. Optionally move the cheap controls-plus-loop figure into the per-PR lane, which today reaches no cycle code.

title: stress.py misses a 2x solve regression in one scenario when the extra work is outside the simulate seams
claim: When one scenario's solve CPU is doubled (winter/2z/dhw at 2.014x) with all the extra work outside the three metered simulate seams, 0 of tests/stress.py's rules trip (ceiling, per-scenario, sweep, evaluations, simulate steps, kernel cost). Candidate: (solve CPU - kernel CPU) per counted evaluation, with the KERNEL_DOUBT re-solve median that kernel_cost_over_verdict uses. Or judge per-scenario solve CPU against that same-machine baseline instead of the recorded table at 3.0x. Also correct the SCENARIO_WORK_FACTOR comment's claim. title: Entry unique id is not re-derived after reauth or an options edit, so the same plant can be set up twice
claim: A fresh setup that submits an entry's current identity answers is accepted as a new entry in 3 of 5 arms. The 3 arms are after reauth, after an options-page token change, and after an options-page indoor-sensor change. In the same 3 arms, a setup with the original answers (which no entry now holds) is refused as already_configured.
mechanism: config_flow.entry_identity hashes the Tibber token and 13 entity slots into the unique id. _async_save_reconfigure re-stamps unique_id. async_step_reauth_confirm and the options 'entities' page (_save_or_menu/_save) write the same identity keys but never update entry.unique_id, so the duplicate guard compares against a stale id.

Better: the id is keyed on an account or home identity that does not rotate with the credential (for example Tibber viewer.userId or home id), which would also let reauth refuse a different account (wrong_account).

title: Optimize-now button press returns normally when the solve did not run; the run_optimization action raises
claim: On the same coordinator state, handle_run_optimization raises HomeAssistantError but ForceOptimizationButton.async_press returns normally, in 2 of 3 input arms (stale prices / no_prices, price feed down). The prices-OK control arm counts 0.

So the #294 refusal that the service implements never reaches a platform action, which the action-exceptions rule covers explicitly.

title: Tibber auth refusal reaches HA as ConfigEntryNotReady/UpdateFailed, never ConfigEntryAuthFailed
claim: In 3 of 3 auth-refusal arms (setup 401, setup 403, steady-cycle 401), the exception the integration delivers is transient-class (ConfigEntryNotReady or UpdateFailed), not ConfigEntryAuthFailed. The integration has 0 ConfigEntryAuthFailed raise sites. The HTTP 500 and connection-error controls are correctly transient (2/2).

The first refresh converts that to ConfigEntryNotReady, so HA retries setup and keeps polling Tibber with a token it knows is revoked, instead of stopping and marking the entry for reauthentication as test-before-setup requires. The stub has no ConfigEntryAuthFailed class and no auth arm in DataUpdateCoordinator._async_refresh, so no test can express the correct behaviour (P11).
phenomenon_property: An authentication refusal from any credentialed fetch reaches Home Assistant as ConfigEntryAuthFailed, at setup and on steady cycles, and the update wrappers never re-wrap it as UpdateFailed. The test stub models ConfigEntryAuthFailed and upstream's auth arm.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed on the reauth verdict and pass it through the two update wrappers. tests/hastub: add the exception and the upstream auth arm in _async_refresh and the first refresh.

Update quality_scale.yaml rows entity-translations/icon-translations accordingly.

title: A code-owned change pushed after the owner approval merges on that stale approval (dismiss_stale_reviews=false)
claim: Ruleset 23698884's pull_request rule has dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push=false and require_last_push_approval=false, so 2 of 201 readable merges since the rule landed (#1621, #1623) merged a code-owned file changed after the owner's last approval, with no approval at the merged head from anyone, although decisions 0008 3(d)/0009 step 6 record the head-moved rule as enforced by GitHub.
mechanism: GitHub keeps an approval across later pushes when dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push is false; require_code_owner_review is then satisfied by an owner approval on an older head. The only in-tree approval-at-head check (budget_raise_gate.py:approval) runs only for budget raises.
phenomenon_property: No pull request may merge with a code-owned path changed after the code owner's last approval; an approval covers only the commit it was given on.
proposed_fix_scope: Owner: set dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push=true (or require_last_push_approval=true) on ruleset 23698884; correct 0008/0009's status if the owner keeps false.

title: A non-stamp direct push to main over the DeployKey bypass is reported by no enumerator
claim: With main-protect-checks' bypass [{DeployKey, actor_id null, always}], a single-parent first-parent commit that is not a stamp's output passes stamp.py:rule4_problem whenever the window also holds one noted PR merge: 0 of 2 injected rows reported, while a two-parent direct merge is reported 1/1.
mechanism: blind_merges only considers parents>=2; enumeration_went_blind fires only when no PR at all was read; policy_lint.mjs's enumerator skips any first-parent with no PR as a stamp. Nothing compares a single-parent commit's files with STAMP_WRITES.
phenomenon_property: Every commit that reaches main without a pull request is either a stamp's output (files within STAMP_WRITES) or is named by a detector.
proposed_fix_scope: rule4_problem refuses a single-parent first-parent commit whose file set is not within STAMP_WRITES (stamp.py, ~5 lines, plus its self-test arm); optionally the same in delivery_status.collect.

title: Three pull_request jobs execute the PR's own code-owned scripts while holding contents:write + actions:write
claim: tests.yml closures-autofix, claims-autofix and mutation-autofix check out head_ref with secrets.CLOSURES_PUSH_TOKEN || github.token (persisted) and then import the PR's own tests/closure.py (and tests/env_drift.py), so PR code runs with a write token before the owner review its code ownership requires.
mechanism: A pull_request run uses the PR's workflow and files; these jobs do not restore the executed scripts from the base as decision 0013 does for pinned graders, and actions/checkout persists the token in .git/config by default.
phenomenon_property: No job holding a write token runs code the pull request controls before review.
proposed_fix_scope: Restore tests/closure.py, tests/env_drift.py, tests/mutation_table.py from pull_request.base.sha before the merge step of the three jobs; persist-credentials: false until the push step. Whether CLOSURES_PUSH_TOKEN is set is unknown (secrets API 403) and should be stated by the owner.

title: Owner approvals given by the orchestrator are indistinguishable from the owner's in GitHub's record
claim: Of 90 tvofi APPROVED reviews on readable merges since 2026-09-17, 29 state in their body that the orchestrator gave them and 46 are empty; budget_raise_gate.py:approval accepts the agent-given approvals as the owner's on 27/27 PRs, so the ruleset's only human-oversight point is not provable from the record.

proposed_fix_scope: Owner decision: delegated approvals under a distinct code-owner identity (second account or a team), or a refusal in budget_raise_gate for delegated approvals; no change is proposed to the mandate itself.

title: Per-file policy caps count lines, so a capped rule file grows in prose with its per-file budget check green
claim: Appending ~150 tokens (600 bytes) of new prose to an existing line of each of 7 zero-headroom capped policy files produces 0 per-file budgets errors from policy_lint.mjs:checkBudgets in 7 of 7 cells, while the same bytes as 8 new lines are refused in 7 of 7.
mechanism: checkBudgets compares r.lines (countLines) against files[<file>]; bytes are only summed into the five aggregate caps, each compared against cap+_band (500 tokens). Line-joining or reflowing therefore buys per-file prose growth bounded only by whatever aggregate band is left -- the silent per-file growth ratchet-budgets.md says the exact per-file comparison exists to prevent ('a band there would buy silent growth in every capped file at once').
phenomenon_property: Every per-file policy cap must bound the file's prose (bytes/tokens), not a quantity a reflow changes without changing the prose.
proposed_fix_scope: Record per-file caps in bytes or tokens (or add a byte cap beside the line cap) in policy_budgets.json and compare them exactly in checkBudgets; ratchet-budgets.md's per-file paragraph then states the unit. Owner approval needed (policy).

title: policy_lint --hooks never reads a hook's matcher: a PreToolUse matcher naming no edit tool passes as wired
claim: With .claude/settings.json's PreToolUse matcher replaced by any of 4 values that match no file-editing tool (Read, Bash, Glob, NoSuchTool), policy_lint.mjs:cmdHooks exits 0 ('HOOKS ok: 3 wired hook(s)') in 4 of 4, although pre-edit.sh would then never run on an Edit/Write.
mechanism: cmdHooks iterates event -> group -> hook, extracts the script path from the command and runs its --self-test; REQUIRED checks only (event, script) pairs. g.matcher is read nowhere, and pre-edit.sh's self-test drives decide() directly, so neither sees the matcher that decides whether Claude Code ever invokes the hook.
phenomenon_property: The hook-wiring check must refuse any settings.json in which a required hook cannot fire on the tool events its rule targets -- event, script AND matcher.
proposed_fix_scope: cmdHooks: add the expected matcher to each REQUIRED row (PreToolUse must match Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) and refuse otherwise; a fixture under fixtures/policy-rot/hooks/ with a wrong matcher pins it. The fix is in D11-s1's file; the defect is observed through my cell settings.json.

title: The owner-approval predicate keys on the tvofi account, and 6 of 6 sampled owner approvals at head were seat-given
claim: Over the 12 first-parent merges before the baseline, budget_raise_gate.approval() -- the in-tree predicate for CLAUDE.md's 'approval is the owner's approving GitHub review' -- counts an owner approval at the merged head on 6 PRs, and all 6 of those reviews state in their own body that the orchestrator seat gave them; 0 human owner approvals at head are distinguishable on GitHub's record.

Under the owner's 12-hour delegation (quoted only in review bodies; no in-tree decision records it -- git grep -il mandate finds none newer than decision 0009) the orchestrator posts reviews with the owner's credentials, so the human-oversight point CLAUDE.md and decision 0013 describe is indistinguishable from a seat's review. NIST AI 600-1/AI RMF GOVERN (accountability, human oversight provable from records) is the bar missed; the delegation itself was the owner's choice.

title: CLAUDE.md rule 1 quotes a mode line the gate does not print, and says FULL prints a zero it does not
claim: Of CLAUDE.md rule 1's two claims about the gate's mode line -- the literal `MODE: SCOPED — 0 script(s) run` and 'MODE: FULL ... prints zero' -- 0 of 2 hold on tests/closure.py:print_plan's output ('MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, ...'; 'MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.').
mechanism: print_plan writes ASCII `--`, CLAUDE.md quotes an em dash; the FULL line carries no count. A seat grepping a log for the quoted literal finds nothing; policy_lint's citations class resolves symbols and paths, not quoted output strings.

title: Hot water without a tank probe: every solve starts from the 55 C ThermalState default, never advanced
claim: With hot water configured and dhw_temp_entity omitted (the config flow's default install), the coordinator hands the solver dhw_temperature = 55.0 C on every cycle. In a 24-cycle closed loop, 23 of 24 solves start more than 1 K away from the tank the integration's own model says it left, and the model-truth tank spends 6.25 h of the demand windows below dhw_min_temperature, against 0 h with the probe mapped.
mechanism: coordinator._update_current_state writes _current_state.dhw_temperature only from an ok reading of CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY (coordinator.py ~5431), and no other producer advances it. So _solve_snapshot deep-copies the ThermalState dataclass default of 55.0 into every solve, and the optimizer uses initial_state.dhw_temperature as the tank's initial temperature. The plan therefore always believes the tank was just charged, schedules little DHW, and the next cycle resets to 55 again. _dhw_probe_temperature already fences this constant away from the display and the learners, but the solver is not fenced. slab_temperature is the same seam when floor_return_temp_entity is omitted: it is seeded once to room+1 K and never advanced (1 distinct solver-initial value in 24 solves, against 23-24 with the probe).
phenomenon_property: A plant-state field whose probe is omitted must not be handed to the solver as a never-advanced constant (a dataclass default or a one-time seed). It must be propagated from the integration's own model between cycles, or marked unknown.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: when dhw_temp_entity (and likewise floor_return_temp_entity for slab_temperature) gives no ok reading, seed the next solve's state from the previous plan's trajectory at the elapsed step (open-loop propagation), instead of leaving the ThermalState default or the one-time seed in place.

title: Untouched Hot water / Hot water tank options page turns hot-water planning on for an install with no tank
claim: On an entry without hot water (the one 'Finish setup now' creates), posting the Hot water page (top menu) or the Hot water tank page (advanced menu) back untouched stores dhw_windows or dhw_tank_volume. The DHW presence rule then enables DHW, and the next solve plans 9 DHW steps (3.16 kWh) for a tank the user never configured.
mechanism: _ABSENT_IS_NOT_DEFAULT (config_flow.py ~2102) exempts CONF_DHW_WINDOWS and CONF_DHW_TANK_VOLUME from _omit_unstored_defaults, so an untouched post of their form defaults is stored. thermal_model._dhw_enabled_from_config treats either key's mere presence as 'hot water configured'. Whether hot water is configured is thus decided by two predicates: the flow's no-op-save rule and the model's presence rule. Visiting and saving an untouched page, the documented back-out path (async_update_options docstring), flips the plant.
phenomenon_property: An untouched submit of any configuration page must not change which plant components (DHW tank, zones, wood tank, valve layout, PV) the model runs. A page's own defaults posted back over an unconfigured component must leave that component unconfigured.
proposed_fix_scope: config_flow.py (and/or thermal_model._dhw_enabled_from_config): an untouched default post of dhw_windows/dhw_tank_volume over an entry without hot water must not be stored as presence, or DHW presence must be an explicit dhw_enabled answer written by the page. The wizard's dhw step (lead to D4-s2) has the same shape.

title: On an on/off pump, the switch path switches off steps whose planned heat the plan books as delivered
claim: The solver treats a step below the modulation floor as duty cycling within the step (bounds [0,P_max], optimizer.py ~:3962). The switch path instead commands ON only at max(0.1, min_electrical_power*0.5) (HeatPumpOptimizer._power_to_heat_pump_schedule and get_current_action; pump_arbiter._on_kw uses the same threshold). On an on/off pump (min==max==6 kW, which config_flow._power_errors accepts) the threshold is 3 kW, so the plan's 1.0-1.4 kW trickle is switched OFF while the trajectory, cost and savings count that heat as delivered. On/off arm: 4/9 cells withhold more than 10% of planned energy. Shoulder withholds 0.671 (8.30 of 12.38 kWh over 30 steps), producing 30 end-to-end switch.turn_off calls on steps with planned heat. Modulating null arm: 0/9 cells (max 0.014) and 0 such calls. Shoulder open-loop consequence: min room 20.64 C planned vs 19.89 C actuated, 17.2 K*h below the plan's own trajectory, 0 K*h below min_temperature.
phenomenon_property: Every seam that decides whether the pump runs a plan step must agree with the solver's reading of a sub-floor step as duty cycling. A step with planned heat must not be actuated OFF.
proposed_fix_scope: Make the on/off decision consistent with the plan for sub-floor steps. Either the threshold stops withholding planned heat (ON when a step carries planned heat, letting the pump's own thermostat duty-cycle), or the solver is constrained to bang-bang or the floor when min==max. The seams listed by the rule change together.

title: The pump-duty arbiter writes the operating mode with select.select_option whatever domain the mode slot holds
claim: topology.ASSIGNABLE_KEYS['heat_pump_mode_entity'] accepts select, sensor and input_select, and config_flow has no check tying pump_duty_mode=control to a writable domain. pump_arbiter._write still hard-codes ('select','select_option'), the defect #1526 fixed for the switch slot via coordinator._on_off_service. Under control with an input_select mode slot, 5 of 5 mode writes are routed to a domain with no such entity. The mode is wrong on all 9 arbitration ticks, and the pump_write_ignored repair tells the user the pump does not hold a write that never reached it, retried every 5 min. A sensor (enum) slot fails the same way. Null control, a select slot: 0 misrouted, 0 wrong ticks, no repair.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.pump_arbiter:_write (driven by pump_arbiter.apply on a real HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator)
phenomenon_property: Every write to a user-assignable slot routes by the assigned entity's own domain. A slot assigned a read-only domain is never written under control; it is refused or declared unavailable rather than retried with a repair.
proposed_fix_scope: pump_arbiter._write routes select_option by the target's domain (select or input_select). Control does not write a sensor mode slot: it skips it or the config flow refuses control with a read-only slot.

title: On an on/off pump every full-power step publishes as 'eco' and power_normalized runs to -60
claim: get_current_action computes p_norm = (P - min)/max(max - min, 0.1). When min==max the 0.1 kW divisor floor turns a degenerate range into a x10 scale. A full-power 6 kW step gets p_norm 0, so HeatPumpActionSensor.native_value is 'eco' rather than 'boost', and idle steps publish power_normalized = -60. On/off arm: 149 full-power steps mislabelled across 7/9 cells (range 0-31, LOO 118); power_normalized minimum -60.0. Modulating null arm: 0 mislabelled; minimum -0.2, which is the same formula on every install and goes as a lead. The climate hvac_action is unaffected because it also reads heat_pump_on.
phenomenon_property: The published action band and power_normalized stay in [0,1] and rank a full-power step at the top on every compressor kind, including min==max.
proposed_fix_scope: get_current_action handles a zero modulation range (an on/off pump is either off or at 1.0) and clamps power_normalized to [0,1].

title: Full config-flow wizard invents a DHW tank and a second zone the user never affirmed
claim: Of the 6 completion paths of the shipping initial config flow, submitted untouched, the 2 full-wizard ('Continue setup') paths create entries whose first coordinator cycle models a 200 L DHW tank. The 'Enter thermal values directly' path also runs the two-zone model. No answer on either path said the house has hot water or two zones; the quick-setup paths answered 'no' produce neither.
mechanism: The presence rules thermal_model._dhw_enabled_from_config (tank volume, thermometer or windows present) and the two-zone 'auto' rule in ThermalParameters.from_config (any zone key present) meet forms that always submit those keys. async_step_dhw offers no 'no hot water' answer and pre-fills dhw_tank_volume=200 and dhw_windows. async_step_zones, whose docstring calls it an 'optional step', pre-fills four zone keys. Only quick_setup.derive writes the explicit dhw_enabled / two_zone_mode flags. On the thermal path the plan covers 26.45 kWh against 22.24 kWh for the stated plant, with predicted_cost 19.289 against 11.796, in the same cycle.
phenomenon_property: A plant (DHW tank, second zone) is modelled only when an answer on the user's own setup path affirmed it. No form default and no key presence alone may turn one on.
proposed_fix_scope: config_flow.py async_step_dhw and async_step_zones: ask 'has DHW' and 'two zones', or write explicit dhw_enabled / two_zone_mode from the answers the way quick_setup.derive does, so that untouched defaults no longer act as presence. Update tests/entities.py's pinned 'turns hot water on anyway' check.

title: --stats API-mode enumerator silently drops 52 of 253 window merges whose /commits/<sha>/pulls answers []
claim: policy_lint.mjs --stats --since v6.6.0 at 1936d5ca reports 201 merged pull requests while main's first-parent history holds 253 `Merge pull request #N` merges, and prints no line naming the 52 it dropped.
mechanism: fetchPullsBySha maps a sha only when /commits/<sha>/pulls returns rows; enumerateMerges (API mode) then skips every unmapped first-parent commit as a stamp. PRs #1098-#1165 return [] (their PR records 404), so their merges vanish from the population and from STATS COVERAGE's denominator without an unfetched/UNCHECKED marker.
instrumented_symbol: .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs:enumerateMerges (via the --stats CLI, fetchPullsBySha over a stub curl replaying the live API)
phenomenon_property: Every first-parent merge commit of a pull request in the window is in the --stats population, or is counted and printed as unfetched; none leaves the denominator silently.
proposed_fix_scope: In API mode treat a first-parent commit whose subject is `Merge pull request #N` and whose /pulls rows are empty as merge #N with unfetchable data: count it, list it on the unfetched line; fetchWindow must record rather than abort on its 404.

title: 22 re-verification rounds after a moved head caught 0 defects; 12 heads moved only by merges or ci: commits
claim: Over v6.6.0..1936d5ca every one of the 22 parsable verdicts re-verifying a head that moved after a `merge` verdict was again `merge` (0 blocked), and 12 of those heads differed from the reviewed one only by merge commits or `ci:` bot commits.
mechanism: An approving verdict binds an exact head, so any move -- including merging main to clear DIRTY or a bot re-record -- costs a full fix-review round; nothing distinguishes a move that changes the branch's diff from one that does not.
phenomenon_property: A review round is spent only where it can catch something: a head move that leaves the branch's diff against its merge base unchanged does not cost a fix-review round.
proposed_fix_scope: A mechanical diff-equivalence check (branch diff vs new merge base byte-identical to the reviewed diff, bot ci: commits excluded) that carries the verdict across a merges-only move; full fix review only when it fails. Policy change: owner approval needed.

title: Body-answer blocks (8) exceed every engineering block class (max 1); record-and-body 12 vs engineering 7
claim: Of the window's 21 blocked verdicts, 8 block because the PR body did not answer a red check (root-cause-unanswered 6, untaught red-check 2) while no engineering class has more than 1, and the record-and-body bucket (12) exceeds engineering (7).
mechanism: The root-cause trigger (a check went red on a branch commit and the body does not name it) is a mechanical predicate over the check-runs listing and the body, yet it is enforced only by the fix reviewer, so each miss costs a full review round.
phenomenon_property: A block whose predicate is mechanical from the API (red check on a branch commit, unnamed in the body) is refused by a check before review, not discovered by a review round.
proposed_fix_scope: A pre-review check (pr-contract lane) that lists check runs concluded failure on the branch's commits and refuses a body that names none of them under the root-cause section; review keeps only the judgement of the answer.

title: P1: a malformed store leaf raises out of a loader or consumer; a naive legionella timestamp wedges every refresh
claim: At baseline, 11 of 4027 single-leaf store mutants (7 seams) raise out of a real loader or consumer. A naive timestamp in dhw_legionella fails 3 of 3 _async_update_data cycles, and none of the 7 seams falls on a leaf that tests/finite_boundary.py substitutes.
mechanism: QuarantiningStore scrubs only non-finite numeric leaves, and finite_boundary.py substitutes only numeric leaves and drives only the loader and _build_data_dict. Stored timestamps are parsed without awareness coercion and compared with the aware dt_util.now(). best_restore calls np.isfinite on an arbitrary leaf, _apply_learner_payloads assumes learners is a dict, and pump_arbiter._load assumes the shape of written.
phenomenon_property: No single-leaf malformation of any persisted store (non-finite, wrong type, naive timestamp, wrong container kind) may raise out of that store's loader or its downstream consumers, or fail an update cycle.
proposed_fix_scope: One shared stored-instant parser that coerces naive to aware, used at every store timestamp read (legionella.async_load, boost._parse_until, pump_arbiter._load, manual_plan.ManualOverride.from_dict, coordinator._maybe_run_fuse_advisor, away._parse_return_time). _as_float in SnapshotRing.best_restore. An isinstance(learners, dict) guard in _apply_learner_payloads and the restore service. Shape guards in pump_arbiter._load. Barrier: fold this detector's writer-driven seeding, all-leaf-kind substitution and consumer/wedge arms into tests/finite_boundary.py, asserting 0 escapes and 0 wedged seams (about 22-26 s gate, provisional).

title: P6: horizon_hours read from coordinator.data but never written; boost probes a field only a test double defines
claim: At baseline, 2 consumer reads of coordinator.data (sensor.py:1482 and :1515, key horizon_hours) are absent in all 10 driven cells and written by no producer, and 1 getattr (boost.py:212 boost_calls) probes a name only tests/harness.py:FakeCoordinator defines.
