instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._build_data_dict (payload wrapped in a recording dict as coordinator.data; every PLATFORM_LIST entity property and diagnostics:async_get_config_entry_diagnostics read)
phenomenon_property: Every key a consumer asks of coordinator.data is written by _build_data_dict in at least one reachable configuration, and every attribute probed with a default is defined by production code or Home Assistant.
proposed_fix_scope: Publish horizon_hours from _opt_config.horizon_hours in the payload, or drop the read. Remove the boost_calls hook from boost.set_channel and have the test double patch persist instead. Barrier: promote p6_keys arms A-C to a tests/ script, or into entities.py, asserting all three counts are 0 (about 10 s gate, provisional).

title: P2: the two-zone and wood-furnace facts are re-derived from a proxy key at three seams beside their canonical predicate
claim: On 40 boundary configurations, config_flow._derive_preset disagrees with ThermalParameters.from_config(...).two_zone_enabled on 20 and modbus_prefill.infer offers a flow target the pre-fill save refuses (or misses one it would accept) on 20; on 21 wood configurations topology.describe_setup's wood tank disagrees with wood_fuel.wood_furnace_on on 2; each drops to 0 when the proxy read is replaced by the canonical predicate.
mechanism: ThermalParameters.from_config decides two_zone_enabled from the explicit two_zone_mode override first and the presence of any of four zone keys second; wood_fuel.wood_furnace_on decides the furnace from its flag first and a fixed inferred-key set second. Three seams decide the same fact themselves: _derive_preset (config_flow.py:1125) and modbus_prefill._plant (modbus_prefill.py:212) test bool(current.get(CONF_UPPER_FLOOR_THERMAL_MASS)), ignoring the mode key, the other three presence keys and a present-but-0.0 value; topology._wood_tank_shown (topology.py:376) re-derives the furnace from a different inferred-key set (adds valve_outlet_temp_entity, drops dhw_wood_coil_enabled). The R7-D12-01 fix (3602b6ca) moved the flow-target guard and the pre-fill save guard to the canonical predicate and left these siblings. Consequence: a two_zone_mode=off install whose zone keys survive in entry.data gets two-zone questionnaire physics written into a single-zone model (house_thermal_mass 0.267x the canonical preset's on the probe house); two_zone_mode=on without an upper-mass key gets single-zone physics (3.75x); the GCHV pre-fill offers a flow write target its own save then refuses; the setup diagram draws a wood tank the model does not run, or hides one it does.
phenomenon_property: Every decision about a presence-inferred configuration fact (two_zone_enabled, dhw_enabled, wood_furnace_on) is made by that fact's canonical predicate (ThermalParameters.from_config / _dhw_enabled_from_config / wood_furnace_on), never by reading one of its proxy keys in a test context outside the predicate.
proposed_fix_scope: Route the three seams through the canonical predicates: _derive_preset and modbus_prefill._plant through ThermalParameters.from_config(...).two_zone_enabled (or a thin two_zone_enabled(config) helper in thermal_model beside _dhw_enabled_from_config), topology.describe_setup through wood_furnace_on (and decide separately whether valve_outlet_temp_entity should join wood_furnace_inferred). Barrier: a tests/entities.py check running the seam rule with a disposition table for the 21 guarded/not-applicable reads, refusing any new decision-context proxy read.

title: P8: a money figure's currency comes from the label source, never from the price feed that denominates it
claim: Over 12 feed-unit x instance-currency cells the current-price sensor publishes the feed's number under hass.config.currency in all 8 cells where the price entity declares a different ISO code, with no repair issue in any; the firewood price widget is the only one of 4 currency-labelled option widgets that ignores the instance currency; and the card names two currencies on one screen for un-converted figures when card-config currency is set (price axis and what-if delta off the install's currency -- 3 counted surfaces, the axis counted as computed and as drawn; 4 before R7-D4-03, the savings table too).
mechanism: inputs.normalize_price_per_kwh parses a price entity's <money>/<energy> unit for its scale and discards the money code ('The currency itself is never converted'); coordinator.currency is currency.resolve_currency(hass), i.e. hass.config.currency, and every money sensor's native_unit_of_measurement and the plan sensors' currency attribute come from it; _audit_price_units only flags an unparseable unit. So an EUR/kWh Nord Pool entity on an SEK instance publishes 0.10 as 0.10 SEK/kWh. The config flow resolves three money widgets through resolve_currency(hass) but CONF_WOOD_PRICE_SEK_M3's widget hard-codes 'SEK/m³' (config_flow.py:1645; also the simulate_plan service description in strings.json/en/sv), and wood_fuel compares that price directly with the plan's electricity prices. The card resolves currency twice: PlanSource.currency() lets card-config currency lead (price axis, what-if delta), savingsUnit() lets the savings sensor's declared unit lead (headline, savings table) -- R7-D4-03 moved only the savings table.
phenomenon_property: Every surface that labels a money figure resolves its currency through one function whose inputs include the currency the number actually arrives in (the price feed's declared code); a mismatch between the feed and the instance is either adopted or raised as a repair issue, never silently relabelled; no money unit is a literal.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: keep the price feed's declared money code (price entity unit, or Tibber's priceInfo currency) beside coordinator.currency and raise a repair issue when they differ (or adopt the feed's, with the statistics-orphan cost currency.py documents); config_flow: the firewood price widget through _ByHass(resolve_currency) and the service description through a {currency} placeholder; card: one resolver for every un-converted money surface (the what-if delta and price axis follow savingsUnit's precedence, or the savings surfaces follow the override -- one rule either way). Barrier: the seam rule as a tests/entities.py check (no literal currency unit in a selector or translation string; every money surface through the one resolver) plus p8_card.mjs's one-screen-one-currency assertion in tests/card.mjs, replacing the card.mjs check that pins 'an explicit card setting still wins' for the delta alone.

title: I4: class roster and finding grammar have disagreeing readers (P11 on no D14 seat; intake admits schema-refused ids)
claim: bugclasses.json has 16 class ids but scopes.json's D14 axis has 15, so P11 is held by no D14 seat while check_scopes.check() reports D14 ok; and audit-find.js's intake, executed on 22 boundary findings, admits 11 that finding.schema.json refuses (class ids P0/P12/P99/I0/I6/P011 and ids D14-s2-1/-001/-xx/-/-01a), 0 after it is rebuilt from the ledger and the schema's id pattern.
mechanism: The class roster is written in four places: the ledger (bugclasses.json), the schema enum (held equal to the ledger by check-wave-script.mjs), the D14 axis in scopes.json (held equal to nothing), and audit-find.js's CLASS_GUESS = /^([PI][0-9]+|new)$/ plus a reportSchema whose class_guess is {type: 'string'}. P11 was added to the ledger and the schema (v6.6.12 root cause) but not to the D14 axis, and check_scopes.py proves completeness against the dimension's own axis, which is the stale list. The intake's id rule is f.id.startsWith(`${seat}-`), not the schema's ^D..(-s[0-9]+)?-[0-9]{2}$. check-wave-script.mjs's intake test uses X9 as its unknown class, a case both readers already agree on.
instrumented_symbol: tools/audit/check_scopes.py:check; .claude/workflows/audit-find.js:CLASS_GUESS and the intake loop it gates (executed in a node vm)
phenomenon_property: Each audit identifier (class id, finding id, dimension, seat, step) has one definition, and every reader either loads it from that definition or is held equal to it by a check that exercises the cases where the readers could differ.
proposed_fix_scope: Add P11 to scopes.json's D14 axis and to a seat; make check-wave-script.mjs (or check_scopes.py) assert the D14 axis equals the ledger ids; build the intake's class and id checks from finding.schema.json (the enum and the id pattern), or pass the schema into the intake; extend check-wave-script.mjs's intake test with P99 and D1-s2-1 cases.

title: P3: 22 quantities are read through a positive floor at one seam and raw at a sibling; no check enumerates them
claim: At the baseline the package holds 22 quantity groups (6 with a raw read used as a divisor, 1 a store capacity: dhw_tank_thermal_mass) that are read through max(Q, c) at one site and raw, or through a different floor, at another. Nothing in the gate enumerates them: the only barrier is tests/features.py's seven arms pinning the eight seams ab71960d repaired, so a new floor elsewhere is not caught.
mechanism: A floor added as a local divide-by-zero guard changes the value one formula reads while its sibling formulas read the raw quantity, so the two formulas disagree whenever Q is below c (R7 D2-01: the buffer's stored energy became C/0.01 of the delivered heat). At the baseline every listed floor is at or below the config schema's minimum for that quantity (spot-checked: cop_nominal floor 1.0 vs schema 1.5; max_electrical_power 0.1 vs 1 kW; DHW 50 L means C=0.058 vs a 1e-6 floor; frsi 0.3 vs 0.3; slab_heat_transfer 1e-6 vs 0.02; peaks_averaged 1 vs 1). So no seam is reachable from the UI today, and that is why this is low.
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer (every module's source as imported, via heatpump_optimizer.__file__); perturbation seam thermal_model:ThermalModel._simulate_step_two_zone
phenomenon_property: A quantity carries one value per evaluation: if any formula floors it, every sibling formula that reads it in the same computation reads the same floored value, or none of them floors it
proposed_fix_scope: Barrier, not product change: land p3_floors.py as a tests/ script, a lint class with an allow-list of the 22 current groups, each tagged guard-only (floor <= schema minimum) and pinned. The check refuses a new group or a floor raised above the quantity's schema minimum. Cost: 1.3 s wall standalone (provisional), no solve.

title: P4: both multi-start seams stop at non-stationary points; 12 of 30 seam calls ship >0.1 % above reachable
claim: Across 24 golden-built cells (1/2-zone x DHW on/off x 6 price profiles, winter_cold), 12 of 30 production _multi_start_minimize calls return an objective more than 0.1 % above what the same routine reaches from its own candidates at a tight stop (max 0.52 %), and 12 of 30 are above a dense seed ladder's result (max 0.89 %). The gap survives the flat-price null in 3 of 4 topologies, so it is the ftol=1e-6 stop on a rugged objective, not a price-bracketing miss.
mechanism: L-BFGS-B at ftol 1e-6 with FD gradients (eps 1e-4) halts at non-stationary points: on two|nodhw|winter_typical the five production candidates refine to 77.72 to 79.16 at the shipped tolerance, and the same five reach 77.43 at ftol 1e-12 (with ABNORMAL line-search exits). The shipped plan is decided by which start happens to stop lowest. Removing the round-7 deep seed re-finds R7 D0-01 exactly (77.884228, the round-7 number).
instrumented_symbol: optimizer:_multi_start_minimize (wrapped with mock.patch.object; both arms call the original; tight arm patches optimizer:_scoped_minimize options)
phenomenon_property: The plan a seam ships is a stationary point of its own objective, within tolerance, reached independently of which structural seed happens to stop first
proposed_fix_scope: Barrier: run p4_seeds.py on the nightly replay (about 10 min on this box, provisional; too slow for the gate) with p4_tol_misses as a ratchet that may only fall. A product fix would be a convergence criterion for _multi_start_minimize, and it must be priced in money (tests/backtest.py:score) and CPU (stress.py) first: round 4 recorded the realised-money control moving the wrong way for a tighter ftol.

title: P5: sysid adoption gate keys on the UA half-width, which barely moves while unmodelled free heat biases UA to -21 %
claim: Driving the production experiment on declared plants whose true free heat differs from the declared internal gains, sysid:adoption_decision admits 3 fits whose true UA error exceeds the gate's own +-10 % bar (worst -21.43 %, blended heat-loss scale moved -7.97 %). The gated half-width moves only 0.0531 -> 0.0685 as the error goes 0 -> -21 %, and falls (0.0531 -> 0.0491) as the error rises to +8 % on the other side.
mechanism: identify_slab ridges G toward gains_prior_kw, which production sets to the declared internal_gains (coordinator SysIdConfig construction). Free heat the house has but the declaration lacks is absorbed 1:1 by the UA column. The #1459 prior term adds a constant in quadrature to the profile half-width; it prices how strong the prior is, not how far the data sit from it. So the gated quantity is almost independent of the bias. Pre-#1459 the same sweep admits 5 over the bar at hw ~1e-4 (the round-7 D7-01 signature) with a -20.98 % blended shift. The fix cut the weight but kept the phenomenon.
instrumented_symbol: sysid:adoption_decision (and sysid:SystemIdentification.identify_slab through step()/_finish on a declared plant)
phenomenon_property: An adoption gate's admit decision must bound the parameter's error against the truth, so admission is non-increasing in any injected bias the fit cannot see, not only in the fit's self-consistency
proposed_fix_scope: Product: price the gains-prior departure into the gate, for example refuse or down-weight when the fitted G sits at the prior while the residual has a mean, or fit G freely with a data-scaled ridge like identify()'s. Barrier: p5_gate.py as a tests/ script (3 s wall, provisional) asserting p5_admitted_over_bar == 0 over the sweep, next to features.py's sysid pins.

title: Eight production seams still do wall-clock datetime arithmetic across DST; the forecast grid lands 60 min off
claim: On every 2025-2027 Europe/Stockholm transition day the real coordinator cycle executes datetime arithmetic at 9 distinct production sites whose result differs from the UTC truth (8 instances plus tariff._window_slot, a wall-clock label by definition), and the worst (_forecast_arrays' step_offset) puts step 0 of the price/weather grid 60 min away from the solve anchor on 42 of 48 cycles.
mechanism: Home Assistant hands every datetime the process-wide ZoneInfo instance; CPython subtracts two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object as naive wall clock, and datetime+timedelta on a zoned value is wall-clock addition. _forecast_arrays computes step_offset=(now-midnight) in wall minutes, then _utc_step_starts walks UTC from midnight by that many steps, so after the transition the grid is 1 h late (spring) or early (autumn) and the plan is priced against the wrong hour for ~21 h. tests/dst_checks.py freezes only 00:07 (offset 0) so it never runs this path.

title: Python closures miss every file a spawned child process reads; select() skips the script on a change to it
claim: 31 (script, file) pairs across tests/doc_claims.py and tests/deployment_shape.py, and 883 across entities.py, features.py and harness_headers.py, are files the script's child processes read that the script's committed closure omits, so closure.select([file]) returns mode scoped with the script skipped; a one-line tests/hastub edit turns deployment_shape.py red while select() skips it.
mechanism: tests/closure.py:_exec_record records a Python script in-process under sys.addaudithook plus sys.modules. A child process's reads never reach the hook, and only the child's argv is kept. The node lane records under strace -f, but the Python lanes do not. tests/closure.py check re-records with the same blind instrument, so the table is checked against itself and cannot flag these seams. Instances: doc_claims.py spawns tests/plan_view.py, whose payload make_model_figures.demand_windows draws; 9 hastub files are missing. deployment_shape.py spawns its own '-P --driver' child, which imports the integration against tests/hastub; its closure holds no hastub file, so 22 are missing.

phenomenon_property: For every selectable script S, every repo file that S's run or any process S spawns opens for reading is in S's measured closure, or closure.select([file]) runs S anyway.
proposed_fix_scope: Barrier in tests/closure.py. On Linux, record a Python script as _record_node_strace records node: wrap --exec-record in strace -f -qq -y -e trace=openat, take the ABSOLUTE path strace -y prints for the returned fd, and union the result with the audit-hook set, which stays for Darwin and for #1309's .pyc attribution. That retires the DRIVEN_BY_OTHERS hand rule's reason. Decide explicitly whether git-internal reads (git grep, git status) count as dependencies; card_drift.mjs's strace already records them. Standing cost falls only on main's closures job, which re-records anyway: 9.4 s strace wall vs 5.9 s recorded audit-hook seconds on the default set (provisional). Partial, cheaper alternative: a _widen rule giving deployment_shape.py all of tests/hastub, and a closure union doc_claims.py <- plan_view.py. That closes today's 31 but not the next child.

title: Mutation ratchet inventory cannot see 528 of 2313 production guard seams; a new guard of those shapes raises it by 0
claim: tests/mutation_table.py:candidates() yields no site on 528 of the 2313 guard seams in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer (52 of 1346 early-exit ifs, 246 of 668 clamps, 230 of 299 threshold ternaries). A new undispositioned guard whose test spans two lines therefore raises unpinned_sites by 0 and ratchet_refusal does not refuse, against +1 and refusal for the same guard on one line.
mechanism: Six single-line operators. GUARD_OFF fires only on an if whose test is on one line, whose line starts with 'if ' and ends with ':', and which has no else; that misses multi-line tests (46), elif (3), a trailing comment after the colon (2) and else branches (1). CLAMP_DROP fires only on a bare min/max with exactly 2 args on one line; that misses numpy/math clamps (179), multi-line calls (63) and 3+ args (4). No operator touches a conditional expression's test. At their pre-fix commits, two of the six ledger I1 instances whose defect is a guard line are of an invisible shape: R5 D3-04 #1312 (the ternary len(positives) >= 2, 076f4a35^) and R5 D3-08 #1316 (np.clip in curve_learning._step_down, 6438f8f6^).
phenomenon_property: Every production guard (early-exit if, clamp, threshold ternary) has a candidate site in mutation_table.inventory(), so unpinned_sites counts it until it carries a disposition, and a new undispositioned guard raises the ratchet.
proposed_fix_scope: Barrier in tests/mutation_table.py:candidates(). GUARD_OFF on any ast.If, rewriting the test's source segment (multi-line and elif included) to False. CLAMP_DROP on np.clip/np.minimum/np.maximum/np.fmin/np.fmax/math.fmin/fmax and on multi-line min/max calls. A seventh TERN operator that replaces a conditional expression's test with True. Mutants become multi-line edits, which per-worker tree copies already allow. Standing cost is AST-only: inventory() takes 3.77 s CPU today and this detector 3.91 s (provisional). The widening adds 528 sites at base and head alike, so no PR is refused by the widening itself, and the nightly burn-in inherits 528 more candidates to drive.

title: hastub Store decodes with stdlib json: 6 of 6 hostile number tokens load where HA's orjson Store drops the file
claim: For 6 stored documents holding one healthy leaf and one hostile number token (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, 1e400, a 401-digit integer, 2**64), QuarantiningStore.async_load over tests/hastub's Store returns a different payload than over Home Assistant's orjson codec in 6 of 6: the stub keeps the healthy sibling in all 6 where Home Assistant loses the whole store in 5, and the stub hands a 401-digit exact int to the loader that Home Assistant never produces.
mechanism: tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/storage.py round-trips through stdlib json, which accepts NaN/Infinity tokens, decodes 1e400 as inf and keeps arbitrary-precision ints. Home Assistant's Store reads with orjson, which refuses those tokens (and >64-bit literals past double range), logs 'Unrecoverable error decoding storage', moves the file aside and returns None. So every store-fuzz verdict through the stub is leaf-level where Home Assistant's is whole-store: the stub-only raises D1-s1 and D1-s2 reported (19 of 250 accuracy mutants; energy and defrost 10**400) come from it, and the whole-store reset a corrupt file causes in Home Assistant is invisible to the suite.
phenomenon_property: The test double for Home Assistant's Store decodes and encodes exactly as Home Assistant's does (orjson; a document it cannot decode loads as None), so a store fuzz through it reports what Home Assistant would do.
proposed_fix_scope: tests/hastub storage.Store: decode with orjson when importable (it is a Home Assistant core dependency) and return None on a decode error; encode NaN as null as orjson does. Re-run tests/finite_boundary.py and the store fuzzers.

title: A learner or arbiter raise on the cycle path fails the solve or the whole cycle and skips actuation and saves
claim: A raise inside ComfortLearner.record_quiet_period makes async_run_optimization return 'solve_failed' with an ERROR traceback on 3 of 3 cycles although the plan was published, and a raise inside pump_arbiter.apply makes _async_update_data fail 3 of 3 cycles and skip 15 of 15 sibling steps (frequency command, pump drive, accuracy and energy saves, drift watch).

phenomenon_property: A fault in a best-effort subsystem called on the cycle path (a learner feed, the pump arbiter) never turns a produced plan into a failed solve and never aborts the cycle's other actuation or saves; it is fenced and logged once like its siblings.

title: Five store writers do not wait for the startup read: a save in that window replaces persisted learned state
claim: When a store's writer runs while its startup load (spawned fire-and-forget in the coordinator's __init__) is still in flight, the restarted coordinator ends with the defaults instead of the persisted state in 5 of 5 stores (energy totals 1234.5 -> 0.0, ledger operation score 77 -> None, house heat-loss scale 1.3 -> 1.0, price-model days seen 2 -> 0, comfort weight 7.5 -> 5.0), while async_set_mode, the one writer that awaits async_wait_for_read, loses nothing.

title: apply_manual_plan accepts expires_at past the horizon: the override owns all 96 steps, the invariant it states is unenforced

title: A solve worker that cannot start (Popen OSError) skips the in-process fallback: no plan, no fallback notice
claim: With subprocess.Popen raising OSError(EAGAIN) when the solve worker is spawned, 0 of 3 cycles publish a plan and no solve_worker_fallback notice is raised, while the same failure re-raised as ProcessWorkerUnavailable yields 3 of 3 plans through the in-process fallback and the notice.

title: A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable while HA holds its valid reading
claim: With the indoor thermometer's state '21.3' valid in Home Assistant but last reported 61, 90, 240 or 480 min ago, the integration's Indoor Temperature sensor is unavailable in 4 of 7 silence cells (available at 5-59 min), and a thermometer that re-writes an unchanged value (last_reported 5 min, last_updated 480 min) stays available, so the gaps come from genuine report silence, not from ignoring last_reported.
mechanism: InputReader._age_gate marks the indoor reading stale once its last_reported/last_updated age exceeds INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[indoor] = 60 min (x staleness scale, default 1.0); reading_ok['upper_floor_temperature'] goes False and _MeasuredTemperatureMixin.available follows it. A thermometer that reports only on change (common for battery Zigbee/BLE sensors: a stable room for hours sends nothing and Home Assistant writes nothing) therefore reads as dead, contradicting const.py's stated intent that the limits are 'generous multiples of a normal reporting interval so that a healthy sensor never trips them'. The user sees history gaps (reported: ~16:30-20:45 and ~03:30-06:15 local, the stable hours); the same stale flag also withholds the reading from the cycle. D1-s5-01's age_of seam (inlet/humidity) ignores last_reported, but this path does not: its re-report arm is available.
phenomenon_property: A measured input whose source entity still holds a valid state in Home Assistant is not published as unavailable merely because a healthy report-on-change device sent nothing for an hour; staleness of such inputs is judged by the source's own availability or a limit its reporting pattern cannot trip. Too-eager question (orchestrator addendum): the guard is too eager exactly for report-on-change thermometers silent over 60 min (4 of 7 cells, every silence >= 61 min); an unchanged value that moves only last_reported does NOT trip it (rereport_unavailable=0 of 1). How often real devices exceed 60 min was not measurable in this container (no device report-interval corpus); the field evidence is the reported gaps in the stable hours (~16:30-20:45, ~03:30-06:15 local).
proposed_fix_scope: inputs.py/const.py: decide staleness of temperature inputs by the source's availability (or a limit sized for report-on-change devices), or keep the reading published while the source is available and only withhold it from learners; the design decision is the owner's.

title: InputReader has no plausibility window: -127 and 85 degC sensor sentinels are delivered as ok on 6 of 6 temperature inputs
claim: InputReader.read delivers the DS18B20 fault sentinels -127 degC and 85 degC as ok readings on all 6 temperature inputs (indoor, outdoor, DHW, floor return, buffer tank, lower floor): 12 of 12 cells, so every consumer (published sensors, learners, the solve's initial state) receives them as measurements.

phenomenon_property: A temperature input outside the physical window of what it measures is refused (reported as a reading problem) at the input boundary, so no consumer receives a sensor fault code as a measurement.
proposed_fix_scope: inputs.py: a per-key plausible range table beside INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES, refused as a named problem ('implausible') in InputReader.read.

title: DHW setpoint advisor prices candidates at the 5.0 degC ThermalState default when no outdoor thermometer is mapped
claim: On a hot-water install without an outdoor thermometer, _dhw_setpoint_sweep prices all 7 candidates at outdoor 5.0 degC (the constructor default) instead of the forecast the plan uses, so the published cost_per_day is off by more than 5 % on 7 of 7 candidates at a -15 degC forecast (worst 52.7 %) and at -5 degC (worst 26.5 %); the recommended setpoint is unchanged.

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._dhw_setpoint_sweep: use the outdoor thermometer while it reads, else forecast_outdoor_now(self._weather_forecast, now), else skip pricing.

title: nightly_ha._async_check_a4 returns inside finally: an in-flight CancelledError or KeyboardInterrupt is swallowed
claim: When the broken-price refresh raises a BaseException the inner handler does not catch (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt) and the recovery refresh then raises, tests/nightly_ha.py:_async_check_a4 returns normally in 2 of 2 arms because of the `return` inside its finally (tests/nightly_ha.py:1274), and CPython 3.14 emits 1 SyntaxWarning compiling the file (PEP 765).

title: Valve Target Recommendation ships disabled where a mixing valve is set, and available-but-unknown where none is

title: Two parsers of a rule's paths: frontmatter disagree on 2 of 6 legal shapes (rules_sync vs policy_lint)
claim: On 2 of 6 probe frontmatters (a trailing YAML comment on a paths entry; a quoted list item under another key) rules_sync.mjs:parse and policy_lint.mjs:rulePaths return different path lists, so the generated .cursor/rules globs and the binding/budget checks read different scopes for one file; 0 of the 10 live rules diverge today.

Neither calls the other, and rules_sync --check compares the .mdc with its own parse, so the divergence passes both checks.

title: entities.py GOV pin reads governance.yml only: a new governance job in 3 of 3 other workflow files passes
claim: The entities.py pin on governance_cost.py's GOV set stays green when a new job is added to pr-contract.yml, budget-raise-gate.yml or budget-raise-gate-rerun.yml (3 of 3), although GOV's own derivation rule names the first two as governance, and rerun-stale-verdict is already a governance job GOV does not name.
mechanism: The pin checks GOV <= all job ids and _workflow_job_ids(governance.yml) <= GOV; the second arm reads only governance.yml, while governance_cost.py's comment derives GOV from governance.yml plus briefs, pr-contract.yml and budget-raise-gate.yml. Jobs in those files are never compared, so the set can go stale unseen (D13-s1 measured 64 s of rerun-stale-verdict missed).
instrumented_symbol: tests/entities.py GOV pin ('the governance-cost GOV set names only jobs the workflow files define, and every governance.yml job'), executed from its own source slice; tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py:GOV

title: Cold-water inlet default held three times: 3 of 5 sites ignore DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP when it moves
claim: With const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP moved from 10.0 to 12.5, 3 of 5 production sites that resolve a cold-water default still deliver 10.0: bare ThermalParameters() (thermal_model.py:469 literal), sysid._sizing_model's plant (via that literal) and dhw_coil_draw_reduction's inlet_temp default (const.DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP).
mechanism: The default is spelled three ways: const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP (from_config and the options flow read it), a bare 10.0 on the ThermalParameters field, and const.DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP, now only a default argument all three call sites override. They agree only because all three are 10.0 today.
phenomenon_property: A configurable default is defined once and every site that falls back to it reads that one definition.
proposed_fix_scope: The ThermalParameters field defaults to const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP; DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP is removed or aliased to it and dhw_coil_draw_reduction's inlet_temp made required (all 3 callers pass it).

title: 4 of 5 ThermalModel per-step scratch members are written every step and read by no production consumer
claim: Across four real solves (winter_single_dhw, dhw_cold_tank, wood_two_tank, wood_coil) production writes _step_dhw_refused, _step_dhw_floor_injected, _step_dhw_draw_kw and _step_wood_refused 31k-167k times each and no production function reads them (0 consumer reads, 0 loads outside thermal_model.py); only tests/features.py does (18 references).
mechanism: The step functions book refused heat, floor injection and the debited draw on the model instance for a consumer that was never written: only _step_buffer_refused is read (simulate_trajectory). The _step_dhw_draw_kw comment says it lets 'energy accounting outside the model' balance the step; nothing outside reads it. D7-s3-01's reach census counts a store as reach, so it cannot see write-only members.
phenomenon_property: Every member production writes is read by some production consumer; state computed only for tests is dead production work.
proposed_fix_scope: Either give the ledgers their production consumer (the energy/refused-heat accounting their comments describe) or return them from the step for the tests that assert conservation instead of storing them on the instance; retarget the 18 features.py references.

title: Constant DHW parameter helpers recomputed ~15-45k times per solve; a per-solve cache saves 3-17 % of CPU
claim: ThermalParameters.dhw_tank_heat_loss_coefficient, dhw_inlet_reference and effective_dhw_draw_pattern are recomputed 4k-11k, 12k-33k and ~98 times per DHW solve for values constant within the solve; memoising them per instance leaves 5 of 5 plans bitwise identical and cuts the capture's thread CPU by 0.026-0.174 (mean 0.094) against a null arm of -0.030..+0.050 (mean -0.001).
mechanism: The DHW step reads the tank loss coefficient (an np.clip on a scalar each call), the inlet reference and, per horizon build, the windowed draw pattern (24 overlap_fraction calls) through properties/methods that recompute from unchanged parameters on every simulated step.
phenomenon_property: A value that is constant within a solve is computed once per solve, not once per simulated step.
proposed_fix_scope: Hoist the three values once per solve (a cached_property invalidated on parameter change, or locals in simulate_dhw_step's caller); scalar math instead of np.clip in dhw_tank_heat_loss_coefficient.

title: stress.py samples 0 of 51 throttling-valve plants; a valve adds 1.3-2.7x solve CPU the gate never sees

The valve branches of the simulate kernels (_simulate_step_two_zone, simulate_trajectory_batch) and smart_write's larger search therefore contribute no row to the budget table, the same UNSAMPLED shape build_case's docstring records for #287's zero-range bounds.

title: Two-zone comfort penalty halves each zone's floor price; shipped plans sit up to 0.46 K below min_temp
claim: On the stock two-zone house (tests/golden.py:make, winter_cold) the shipped plan's upper zone falls below min_temp 17.0 by 2.467 degree-steps summed over 12 price x DHW cells (1.314 in two|dhw|winter_typical, coldest 16.54 C), while the same house single-zone breaches 0.147 and every flat-price cell 0.
mechanism: _comfort_terms (and _comfort_terms_batch) average the two zones' penalties with 0.5 x (...), which also halves each zone's quadratic floor term and its _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 linear term; the constant's own comment says 2.0 is the smallest L1 that removes residual floor violations, so each zone of a two-zone house gets half of it and the solver buys the breach back where prices reward it (two|dhw|winter_typical: holding the floor costs 70.52 vs 67.50 SEK).
instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize (shipped upper/lower_temp_trajectory), via optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer._comfort_terms / _comfort_terms_batch and the module constant _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1
phenomenon_property: Each zone of a two-zone plan pays the same price per degree-step below min_temp as a single-zone room does, so the floor the L1 term exists to pin holds per zone.
proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py _comfort_terms/_comfort_terms_batch: keep the two-zone average for the pull and the overshoot, but price each zone's undershoot (quadratic and L1) at the single-zone weight; pin with a two-zone winter_typical floor check.

title: Setup overview page and setup diagram publish English slot text on a Swedish install
claim: With the Swedish translation active, 22 of the 23 text lines the setup_overview flow page renders, all 16 slot labels describe_setup publishes (setup_topology, drawn verbatim by the card) and all 3 sensor_advisor labels are byte-identical to the English install's, while the narrative on the same plan sensors is Swedish (0 of 1 identical).

title: sysid cannot adopt its own exact noise-free fit on 43 of 80 preset houses, yet arms on all 80
claim: Driving the production step experiment on a plant exactly equal to the declared one with a noise-free reading, over every BuildingPreset structure x era x emitter at 3.5 and 6 kW, 19 of 80 cells complete and are refused by adoption_decision (heat-loss half-width 0.096-0.234 against the ln 1.10 = 0.0953 bar, fit error 0.0000) and 24 abort as 'fitted parameters outside plausible bounds'; all 80 arm.
mechanism: The adoption bar keys on slab_ua_adoption_halfwidth, which at zero noise is set by the prior and window design, not by the fit's error, so light, radiator-heated and low-energy houses never reach it; separately the fit's plausibility box (tau 0.1-200 h, UA 0.01-5) rejects exact-data fits on masonry, low-energy and slab-floor cells (not separated here: true parameters outside the box versus a fit that misses them).
phenomenon_property: A sysid experiment the tree arms on a declared plant can adopt its own exact answer: at zero bias and zero noise the gate admits and the plausibility box contains the fit.
proposed_fix_scope: sysid.py: arm only where the declared plant's zero-noise half-width clears the bar and its parameters lie in the plausibility box (refuse at arm time with a reason), or size the window/step so they do; widen the box to the presets' own range.

title: Grid-fee bounds are SEK numbers: a 0.05 EUR/kWh fee is unenterable in HUF, ISK, JPY and KRW
claim: A 0.05 EUR/kWh transfer fee converted into each of 12 instance currencies draws 8 blocking verdicts across 4 currencies (HUF, ISK, JPY, KRW): the rules text is refused as implausible (HUF, KRW), the fixed-fee field's selector caps it at 5 in any currency (all four), and an entity-mode fee raises the grid_fee_magnitude repair (HUF, KRW); SEK, EUR, NOK and DKK draw 0.

proposed_fix_scope: grid_fee.py/config_flow.py/coordinator.py: derive the implausibility bound and the fixed-fee selector max from the instance currency (a per-currency scale, or a bound relative to the published spot prices) rather than SEK constants.

title: README's SEK currency fallback is unreachable under Home Assistant core, which defaults Config.currency to EUR
claim: README.md says money is labelled 'SEK when the instance has none', but resolve_currency returns FALLBACK_CURRENCY for 0 of 2 Home Assistant core versions (2025.2.0, hacs.json's minimum, and 2026.2.3): core's Config.__init__ sets currency 'EUR', so an instance that never chose a currency is labelled EUR; only the test stub (FakeHass, currency 'SEK') produces SEK.

phenomenon_property: What the README and currency.py say an unconfigured instance shows is what Home Assistant core delivers, not what the test stub pins.

title: Store-parser non-finite guards in flow_lift, tariff, price_model survive deletion: no gate driver notices
claim: Deleting any of four isfinite guards in persisted-state parsers (flow_lift.py:210, tariff.py:402, price_model.py:324, price_model.py:349) leaves every driver of the file's measured closure, env_drift --all included, green, although each mutant restores corrupt stored values as live state.

instrumented_symbol: flow_lift:FlowCurveBias.from_dict, tariff:PeakTracker.from_dict, price_model:PriceShapeModel.from_dict (via tests/mutation_table.py:killed over each closure driver)
phenomenon_property: Every non-finite/negative-count guard at a persisted-state parser boundary of the solver-side modules is pinned: deleting it turns at least one gate driver red.
proposed_fix_scope: tests only: extend the corrupt-payload checks in tests/features.py (FlowCurveBias, PeakTracker window_factor, PriceShapeModel shapes and quarter_factors) with float()-parseable non-finite strings and a negative sample count, each asserting the inert restore; re-run prescreen --only on the four sites to show the kill.

title: PriceShapeModel residual_var restore can discard every stored variance with the gate green
claim: Replacing price_model.py:368's max(0.0, float(v)) with 0.0 zeroes every restored residual variance, and all 15 closure drivers (env_drift --all included) stay green.
mechanism: The only residual_var load check (tests/features.py:41446) feeds a corrupt 'x' payload and compares to a fresh (all-zero) model, which the mutant also satisfies; no positive-control round trip (learned -> as_dict -> from_dict) asserts a variance survives a restart.
phenomenon_property: Every learned field a persisted-state parser restores is pinned by a round-trip check that fails when the restore discards it.
proposed_fix_scope: tests only: a residual_var (and quarter_factors) round-trip positive control in tests/features.py.

title: Every gate driver runs with process local time = UTC, so open_meteo's naive-stamp UTC guard is deletable
claim: Deleting open_meteo._parse_block's `if parsed.tzinfo is None:` guard (open_meteo.py:209) leaves all 14 drivers of the file's measured closure green, because no lane runs with a non-UTC process TZ; under TZ=Europe/Stockholm tests/open_meteo.py fails 14 checks on the same mutant.
mechanism: The guard makes Open-Meteo's naive ISO stamps explicit UTC; without it `.astimezone(timezone.utc)` reads them as process-local time. The gate's processes are UTC (CI runner, this box), where the two coincide; HASTUB_TZ sets only the stub's DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE, not the process TZ. A Home Assistant container whose TZ is the user's zone would shift every solar sample by the UTC offset.
phenomenon_property: A production guard that normalises a naive datetime to UTC is distinguishable from its deletion only in a process whose local zone is not UTC; the gate never runs one.
proposed_fix_scope: Tests only: run tests/open_meteo.py (or the whole gate's fast lane) once with a non-UTC process TZ, e.g. a run.sh lane or a subprocess arm with TZ=Europe/Stockholm.

title: DrawStats.from_dict can zero the open draw occurrence and no gate check notices
claim: Replacing dhw_draws.py:136 `stats._open_kwh = max(0.0, float(...))` with `stats._open_kwh = (0.0)` survives all 16 pre-screen drivers plus edge.py and backtest.py, while a shower in progress at 1.5 kWh then closes after a store round trip as a 0.0 kWh event instead of 1.5.
mechanism: tests/features.py 'the statistics survive a store round trip' builds its fixture ending with fold('', 0.0), so the occurrence is closed and open_kwh is 0 on both sides of the round trip; the fuzz checks assert only >= 0 or == 0 for malformed input. The restore of a positive open_kwh — the restart-mid-shower case the adjacent comment names — is unpinned.
phenomenon_property: A positive open draw occurrence persisted by DrawStats.as_dict must be restored by from_dict with its energy; no check drives the round trip with open_kwh > 0.
proposed_fix_scope: Tests only: a features.py round-trip check with an open occurrence of positive energy.

title: MonthlyLedger.add's non-finite guard is unpinned; one NaN amount loses the month on reload
claim: Deleting ledger.py:117's `if not (np.isfinite(kwh) and np.isfinite(sek)): return` survives all 13 drivers, finite_boundary.py among them, while one NaN amount after a finite one leaves the month line at kwh=nan and the month is dropped whole by from_dict after an orjson store round trip (1 month kept unmutated, 0 mutated).
mechanism: finite_boundary.py substitutes non-finite values into STORED leaves and checks the loader; no check drives a non-finite amount through the writer, whose guard is the only thing keeping it off disk, where _clean_month then refuses the whole month.
phenomenon_property: A non-finite amount handed to MonthlyLedger.add must leave the month's lines finite; no check hands one to the writer.
proposed_fix_scope: Tests only: a finite_boundary.py or features.py arm that calls add() with nan/inf and asserts the month survives a store round trip.

title: No gate check observes a positive draw folded by DhwProfileLearner.async_fold_draw_stats
claim: Both the seeded mutant (dhw_learning.py:379's external-heat skip deleted: 0.4396 kWh folded during a wood burn instead of 0.0) and a stronger one (`if True:`, so the method never folds anything) leave every driver green; features.py's two checks that drive the method pass on 0 == 0.
mechanism: 'a folded draw's energy is proportional to the tank's own capacity' compares fold_5 and fold_200 with abs(a-b) < 1e-9, and 'a drop that is all standby loss books no draw' asserts == 0.0; neither asserts a positive fold, so a method that folds nothing satisfies both. The external-heat sibling seam in _record_accuracy is pinned; this one is not.
phenomenon_property: A check that drives async_fold_draw_stats must observe a positive folded energy for a beyond-standby drop, and none for an external-heat interval; today no check observes a positive fold at all.
proposed_fix_scope: Tests only: give the two features.py checks a positive control (fold_200 > 0) and add an external_heat_active=True arm expecting no fold.

title: The disinfection write-failed notice memo is unpinned
claim: Deleting legionella.py:453's `if switch.failed == self.write_failed_notice: return` survives all 14 drivers; five healthy observe cycles then issue 5 issue-registry deletes of dhw_disinfection_write_failed instead of 0.
